title: 腾讯财报点名，玩家挤爆现场，这款海外大作靠什么抓住玩家
text:
回应一切信号
如果你要问我上周末，对《 Warframe 》（星际战甲）在中国首次举办的TennoVIP印象最深的是什么？
我会告诉你，不是精美的战甲COS，不是多样的活动，也不是主创登台，而是 各式各样的实体版“妈耶精华” 。
无论是官方活动中的糖画、剪纸、印刷和巨大的人偶服，还是官方为此次活动特意推出的西安肉夹馍版本，亦或是玩家手中各具特色、甚至突破我想象力的各种“妈耶精华”，都让我印象深刻。
作为《Warframe》中国玩家社区中最具辨识度的形象之一，“妈耶精华”已经被玩家开发出无数种变种。 但过去更多还是在线上品鉴，它们是表情包、是图片，只有当你亲身来到线下， 沿着会场走上一圈， 切实摸到和看到，才真正能理解它为何能成为 Tenno 之间心照不宣的暗号。
活动期间，竞核也有幸采访到了《Warframe》创意总监Rebecca、社区总监Megan、中文社区经理Zi，以及来自腾讯 Level Infinite 下负责 DE Partner Team 的 负责人Fred和Level Infinite国内发行业务负责人Kiai。我们谈到了玩家意见如何进入研发流程， 研发认为的 游戏最大的优势，也谈到了中国社区里的梗，以及腾讯与DE之间合作情况等等。
说实话， 在来到线下之 后我才发现 ， 与刻板印象不同 ，现场的年轻玩家远比我想象的多得 多 。而要理解一款 海外长青 游戏为何仍能保持这样的活力，或许要先从 TennoVIP 、校园行 这两场气质截然不同的活动说起。
两场活动，社区的两种面孔
对于《Warframe》的玩家来说，TennoVIP并不陌生。过去，DE会带着开发团队前往不同地区，与当地玩家见面。这一次，它首次落地中国西安，并由DE与腾讯共同完成。
西安的 TennoVIP更像是一次核心社区聚会。玩家带着自制作品来到现场，也带来了个人积“怨”已久的问题。在官方收集的二十多个问题中，内容从游戏更新、玩法机制到角色塑造，IP联动，产品周边等等，话题有大有小，有些问题甚至称得上尖锐。
而Rebecca、Megan以及Zi就坐在玩家面前直接回答，甚至为了保证玩家能够理解，腾讯还贴心的为每一个玩家都准备了同传耳机。Kiai在采访中还提到，这些问题他们都没有提前告诉团队，从玩家那收集到什么，只要是合理的他们就写什么，以真实传达玩家对游戏的想法。
在随后的玩家现场提问环节，问题则更加直接。有玩家当面开炮，质询国服为什么相比国际服少了装备，少了六千多经验？国服未来到底还有没有机会补回来？还有玩家询问，明神到底什么时候才能迎来加强，你们内部到底怎么决定加强谁等等。
Rebecca等人真诚地回答了每一个问题，对于国服少装备的事情，她坦诚地表示会回去查询，然后和团队商量尽量补给大家。能做的事情，她会承诺推进；犹豫的问题，她想要更多玩家们的看法；难以推进的，则坦然表达难处与担忧。
这场数百人的见面会，没有敷衍，没有虚话、套话。有的只是想要更了解玩家的团队，与一群想要知道开发组想法的玩家，而腾讯便是其中的连接双方的桥梁。
在Kiai看来，像“ 星际仓鼠 ”“妈耶精华”并非官方创造，而是玩家社区自发形成的，但他们和玩家的理念是一样的。他们要做的就是把玩家喜闻乐见的梗稳稳接住。
这也是腾讯与DE合作中一个容易被忽视的部分：双方连接的不只是产品和渠道，还有两套不同的文化语境。
第二天的“天诺学院”校园行无疑是另一种气氛，活动于老城根G Park举行。与首日的核心玩家聚会相比，这场活动也面向路过的公众开放。
在现场，我跟着活动参加 战甲 竞速、射击等项目，集齐全部印章，又坐在台下看到冠军的诞生。在活动周围既有一眼就能认出角色和装备的 超级仓鼠 ，也有被战甲Coser和舞台比赛吸引、临时停下脚步的家庭。
对这些路过的观众而言，他们或许不知道这是什么游戏，也不知道上面的玩家在干什么，但他们能直观的感受到，这些战甲好帅，画面里的角色移动的好快，从而产生一种不明觉厉。
当下或许还不足以让他们入坑，但已经埋下了一颗动作射击游戏的种子，在未来的某一时刻，他们或许就会想起来有这样一个游戏，被蓬勃的社区文化所吸引，然后加入这个游戏。
两场活动面对的是不同人群，却共同呈现了《Warframe》社区的两面：一边是玩家经过十多年积累形成的内部语言、共同记忆和抽象二创；另一边则是游戏如何通过更低门槛的现场体验，继续接触年轻玩家和新用户。
这种将团队的社区沟通优势和产品特色传递给更多玩家，广而告知的能力正是腾讯的强项。也不难怪Fred将合作团队称为“Fuel”，也就是所谓的“燃料”。
在他看来，DE原本就擅长与社区沟通，也具备全球发行和连接地区玩家的能力；腾讯所做的，是利用自身积累的区域发行和用户连接经验，放大DE已经在做的事情，让它触达更多玩家。
独特的产品+玩家的信任 = 长青密码
如今，《Warframe》全球累计玩家数已超过8500万，去年更是登上了腾讯的财报当中被点名表扬。而比这个数字更值得讨论的，则是它 现在 依旧能够吸引新玩家加入的原因。
对此，我们也向Rebecca发出了提问。Rebecca的答案非常的直接和简单：“我们成功的关键主要是玩家的信任以及快速响应的能力。”
她坦言，玩家们确实有很多的诉求，这些诉求的工作量也都非常大。但这并不是他们偷懒的理由，他们一直以来都在努力工作，尽力快速地回应玩家们，而这也是他们最特别，也是最独到的地方。此外她还表示，他们也会持续致力于让游戏保持好玩、刺激、充满惊喜，把玩家喜欢的东西快速地带给他们。
Kiai则从产品本身给出了回答， 她 认为《Warframe》本身就是独特的。无论是游戏的偏星际的题材，还是动作射击的玩法，都是目前国内，甚至全球一流的存在。而更特别的则是DE一直深耕而且非常坚持，也非常听劝，他们自己还在不断地进步，他们的学习也没有停止。
“项目不断进步，真实听取玩家反馈，重视并快速回应”，这听起来几乎是所有长线游戏都会说的话。但关键在于落地，玩家的这些诉求，这些反馈最终能否进入制作流程，以及开发团队能不能调整。
为此，Megan还向我们举了一个“ 原子摩托车 ”的例子。原子摩托车在“ 1 999”版本推出后，曾因为一个Bug出现在各种任务中，甚至能被玩家骑到世界以外的场景。按照一般的开发逻辑，既然这一表现偏离了原始设计，团队应当尽快将其修复。
但玩家非常喜欢这个Bug，因为这太酷太帅了。它确实可能带来一些问题，也不符合最初的设计规则，但DE最终没有简单地将其修复掉，相反他们把Bug变成了正式功能。于是，玩家现在可以骑着原子摩托车进入沃尔上尉的任务，也能把它带到更多想去的地方。
“我们会尽量理解玩家为什么喜欢这些东西。”Megan说，“在迎合玩家诉求方面，我们也要时不时打破常规，尽量去做出让玩家满意的东西。”
到底什么是中国玩家喜欢的东西，中文社区经理Zi在其中则扮演了重要角色。Megan提到，Zi会帮助她了解中国玩家的喜好，也会解释中国社区为什么偏爱某个机制或模式。相比“玩家喜欢什么”，DE更需要理解的是“玩家为什么喜欢”。
“妈耶精华”就是一个例子。
如果只看形象本身，海外开发者很难理解它为什么会在中国社区中成为标志性符号，更难预测玩家能围绕它发展出多少种二创。但经过Zi的整理和解释，Megan已经知道它在中国玩家中的特殊地位，也开始思考可以围绕它做哪些有趣的内容 ,这也是此次肉夹妈耶的由来。
Z i 告诉竞核，她平时还会“潜水”在玩家QQ群里，观察大家的一举一动。TennoVIP当天凌晨5点，她就发现群里已经有了动静，自己也因为兴奋只睡了两个多小时。这种工作没有太多宏大的部分，但玩家意见与内心的真实想法正是通过这些QQ群、视频网站和线下活动进入团队视野，并进一步走进制作流程。
相同的逻辑也体现在内容叙事中。除了大型版本外，团队也会通过各种小任务、短片和剧情铺垫补全角色。Megan告诉我们，她在《Warframe》里最喜欢的事情之一，就是在整个《Warframe》产品里面把角色的故事给塑造好，不管是熟悉的角色还是新角色，把他们融入整个游戏的生态当中。
事实上，很多玩家愿意留下，也并非因为游戏从未出错，是因为他们相信，自己的反馈有人在听。信任也正是在一次次回应、修改和兑现中建立的。
这种与社区玩家建立起沟通与信任，支持玩家的价值观，在Fred看来，正是腾讯和DE合作中，双方达成的第一个、也可以说是最核心的契合点。
看见中国元素，理解中国故事
如果说，两场截然不同的活动体验，让我对游戏的未来充满信心；那么主创团队在交流中对中国元素，中国故事发自内心的喜爱，则让我对游戏在中国的未来充满想象。
过去几年里，不难发现DE对中国玩家越来越重视。
在游戏内容上，他们曾从中国神话中汲取灵感，推出悟空、哪吒等国风战甲；在社区沟通上，团队也开始在国内发布月度答疑、开发者互动日记等互动内容。随着腾讯与DE合作深入，中国社区的意见也有了更直接、稳定的渠道进入开发团队。
但对于“国风内容”，许多玩家的心情其实是很复杂的。
一方面，玩家肯定希望在游戏中能够看到更多熟悉的文化元素，不然也不会每天盼着官方 透 露点嫦娥的新消息，每次都询问有没有“天庭三大反骨的最后一骨——杨戬”的计划安排。但另一方面，越是在意，便越容易担心。海外团队能否真正理解中国故事？所谓的国风内容，会不会只是一次商业层面的示好？
特别是随着文化内容的深入，如“嫦娥”这类不是战斗角色，却拥有更多文化背景或精神的角色逐步公布后。有人期待DE的发挥，也有人担心文化理解上的偏差，最终会让内容停留在表面，甚至产生“还不如不做”的结果。
但此次采访则让我看到，DE并不是出于任务或者要求，而是发自内心的尝试理解和欣赏中国的文化和故事。
活动前，主创团队不仅参观了兵马俑，也观看了“赳赳 大 秦” 的演出等等。Rebecca对演出中 天气配合剧情 变化 的 呈现方式 赞不绝口，并希望能在游戏里也增加类似的体验。兵马俑更是她印象最深的内容，她甚至当场表示未来大家应该会看到一些灵感源于兵马俑的内容。
而Megan则向我们表示，她印象最深刻的是一场以武则天为主题展开的国风晚宴，他们身穿汉服边吃饭，边观看演出。无论是武则天本身的 服饰 ，还是其背后的故事都给她带来了非常大的震撼。女皇、皇帝、兵和马等战斗元素更是给了她许多的灵感。
这种兴趣也体现在一些很小的细节里。
Rebecca告诉我们，她的中文老师当天也来到了活动现场。在交流过程中，她更是不断尝试用中文与我们对话。她的中文当然谈不上熟练，有时只是一句简单的问候，或者夹在英文回答中的几个词，但也正因为如此，这种略显笨拙的尝试反而显得真实。
此次西安之行，也让我重新理解了腾讯与DE在中国市场的合作。活动不仅面向玩家，同样也是给团队一次更好了解中国文化的机会。
社区梗的翻译只是第一步。当合作进一步进入内容和文化层面，只知道某个符号“很受欢迎”显然还远远不够。为此，除了参观兵马俑、观看演出，腾讯还特意邀请主要研究方向为古代神话与文学及中国艺术史的同济大学人文学院教授李晨，与DE交流传统文化，帮助他们理解嫦娥等文化形象背后的文化内涵。
在采访最后，Rebecca已经开始计划下一次中国之行。她想去重庆，也想去成都，还提前向玩家提出要求：“给我准备辣的，但Megan不要辣。”她甚至希望玩家能帮忙说服腾讯团队，把下一次访问安排在成都。
Megan则感谢中国玩家社区欢迎他们来到中国，让他们有机会体验和了解中国文化。Zi也请玩家继续期待接下来的内容。
至于说DE最终能否做好嫦娥的内容，答案仍然要留给正式内容。一次线下活动无法消除玩家对文化理解偏差的担忧，团队表现出的兴趣，也需要通过未来的作品得到验证。
但这次活动至少说明，《Warframe》之所以还能保持年轻，不是它知道所有正确答案。更重要的可能是，面对一个暂时无法理解的梗、一种陌生的文化，或者一个意外出现的Bug，它至今仍然愿意来到玩家身边，继续问一句：
为什么大家会喜欢它？

我会告诉你，不是精美的战甲COS，不是多样的活动，也不是主创登台，而是各式各样的实体版“妈耶精华”。
 
无论是官方活动中的糖画、剪纸、印刷和巨大的人偶服，还是官方为此次活动特意推出的西安肉夹馍版本，亦或是玩家手中各具特色、甚至突破我想象力的各种“妈耶精华”，都让我印象深刻。
 
 
作为《Warframe》中国玩家社区中最具辨识度的形象之一，“妈耶精华”已经被玩家开发出无数种变种。但过去更多还是在线上品鉴，它们是表情包、是图片，只有当你亲身来到线下，沿着会场走上一圈，切实摸到和看到，才真正能理解它为何能成为 Tenno 之间心照不宣的暗号。
 
 
活动期间，竞核也有幸采访到了《Warframe》创意总监Rebecca、社区总监Megan、中文社区经理Zi，以及来自腾讯Level Infinite下负责DE Partner Team的负责人Fred和Level Infinite国内发行业务负责人Kiai。我们谈到了玩家意见如何进入研发流程，研发认为的游戏最大的优势，也谈到了中国社区里的梗，以及腾讯与DE之间合作情况等等。
 
说实话，在来到线下之后我才发现，与刻板印象不同，现场的年轻玩家远比我想象的多得多。而要理解一款海外长青游戏为何仍能保持这样的活力，或许要先从TennoVIP、校园行这两场气质截然不同的活动说起。

两场活动，社区的两种面孔
 
对于《Warframe》的玩家来说，TennoVIP并不陌生。过去，DE会带着开发团队前往不同地区，与当地玩家见面。这一次，它首次落地中国西安，并由DE与腾讯共同完成。
 
 
西安的TennoVIP更像是一次核心社区聚会。玩家带着自制作品来到现场，也带来了个人积“怨”已久的问题。在官方收集的二十多个问题中，内容从游戏更新、玩法机制到角色塑造，IP联动，产品周边等等，话题有大有小，有些问题甚至称得上尖锐。
 
 
而Rebecca、Megan以及Zi就坐在玩家面前直接回答，甚至为了保证玩家能够理解，腾讯还贴心的为每一个玩家都准备了同传耳机。Kiai在采访中还提到，这些问题他们都没有提前告诉团队，从玩家那收集到什么，只要是合理的他们就写什么，以真实传达玩家对游戏的想法。
 
 
在随后的玩家现场提问环节，问题则更加直接。有玩家当面开炮，质询国服为什么相比国际服少了装备，少了六千多经验？国服未来到底还有没有机会补回来？还有玩家询问，明神到底什么时候才能迎来加强，你们内部到底怎么决定加强谁等等。
 
Rebecca等人真诚地回答了每一个问题，对于国服少装备的事情，她坦诚地表示会回去查询，然后和团队商量尽量补给大家。能做的事情，她会承诺推进；犹豫的问题，她想要更多玩家们的看法；难以推进的，则坦然表达难处与担忧。
 
 
这场数百人的见面会，没有敷衍，没有虚话、套话。有的只是想要更了解玩家的团队，与一群想要知道开发组想法的玩家，而腾讯便是其中的连接双方的桥梁。
 
在Kiai看来，像“星际仓鼠”“妈耶精华”并非官方创造，而是玩家社区自发形成的，但他们和玩家的理念是一样的。他们要做的就是把玩家喜闻乐见的梗稳稳接住。
 
这也是腾讯与DE合作中一个容易被忽视的部分：双方连接的不只是产品和渠道，还有两套不同的文化语境。
 
第二天的“天诺学院”校园行无疑是另一种气氛，活动于老城根G Park举行。与首日的核心玩家聚会相比，这场活动也面向路过的公众开放。
 
 
在现场，我跟着活动参加战甲竞速、射击等项目，集齐全部印章，又坐在台下看到冠军的诞生。在活动周围既有一眼就能认出角色和装备的超级仓鼠，也有被战甲Coser和舞台比赛吸引、临时停下脚步的家庭。
 
 
对这些路过的观众而言，他们或许不知道这是什么游戏，也不知道上面的玩家在干什么，但他们能直观的感受到，这些战甲好帅，画面里的角色移动的好快，从而产生一种不明觉厉。
 
当下或许还不足以让他们入坑，但已经埋下了一颗动作射击游戏的种子，在未来的某一时刻，他们或许就会想起来有这样一个游戏，被蓬勃的社区文化所吸引，然后加入这个游戏。
 
 
两场活动面对的是不同人群，却共同呈现了《Warframe》社区的两面：一边是玩家经过十多年积累形成的内部语言、共同记忆和抽象二创；另一边则是游戏如何通过更低门槛的现场体验，继续接触年轻玩家和新用户。
 
这种将团队的社区沟通优势和产品特色传递给更多玩家，广而告知的能力正是腾讯的强项。也不难怪Fred将合作团队称为“Fuel”，也就是所谓的“燃料”。
 
在他看来，DE原本就擅长与社区沟通，也具备全球发行和连接地区玩家的能力；腾讯所做的，是利用自身积累的区域发行和用户连接经验，放大DE已经在做的事情，让它触达更多玩家。

独特的产品+玩家的信任=长青密码
 
如今，《Warframe》全球累计玩家数已超过8500万，去年更是登上了腾讯的财报当中被点名表扬。而比这个数字更值得讨论的，则是它现在依旧能够吸引新玩家加入的原因。
 
对此，我们也向Rebecca发出了提问。Rebecca的答案非常的直接和简单：“我们成功的关键主要是玩家的信任以及快速响应的能力。”
 
她坦言，玩家们确实有很多的诉求，这些诉求的工作量也都非常大。但这并不是他们偷懒的理由，他们一直以来都在努力工作，尽力快速地回应玩家们，而这也是他们最特别，也是最独到的地方。此外她还表示，他们也会持续致力于让游戏保持好玩、刺激、充满惊喜，把玩家喜欢的东西快速地带给他们。
 
 
Kiai则从产品本身给出了回答，她认为《Warframe》本身就是独特的。无论是游戏的偏星际的题材，还是动作射击的玩法，都是目前国内，甚至全球一流的存在。而更特别的则是DE一直深耕而且非常坚持，也非常听劝，他们自己还在不断地进步，他们的学习也没有停止。
 
“项目不断进步，真实听取玩家反馈，重视并快速回应”，这听起来几乎是所有长线游戏都会说的话。但关键在于落地，玩家的这些诉求，这些反馈最终能否进入制作流程，以及开发团队能不能调整。
 
为此，Megan还向我们举了一个“原子摩托车”的例子。原子摩托车在“1999”版本推出后，曾因为一个Bug出现在各种任务中，甚至能被玩家骑到世界以外的场景。按照一般的开发逻辑，既然这一表现偏离了原始设计，团队应当尽快将其修复。
 
 
但玩家非常喜欢这个Bug，因为这太酷太帅了。它确实可能带来一些问题，也不符合最初的设计规则，但DE最终没有简单地将其修复掉，相反他们把Bug变成了正式功能。于是，玩家现在可以骑着原子摩托车进入沃尔上尉的任务，也能把它带到更多想去的地方。
 
 
“我们会尽量理解玩家为什么喜欢这些东西。”Megan说，“在迎合玩家诉求方面，我们也要时不时打破常规，尽量去做出让玩家满意的东西。”
 
到底什么是中国玩家喜欢的东西，中文社区经理Zi在其中则扮演了重要角色。Megan提到，Zi会帮助她了解中国玩家的喜好，也会解释中国社区为什么偏爱某个机制或模式。相比“玩家喜欢什么”，DE更需要理解的是“玩家为什么喜欢”。
 
“妈耶精华”就是一个例子。
 
如果只看形象本身，海外开发者很难理解它为什么会在中国社区中成为标志性符号，更难预测玩家能围绕它发展出多少种二创。但经过Zi的整理和解释，Megan已经知道它在中国玩家中的特殊地位，也开始思考可以围绕它做哪些有趣的内容,这也是此次肉夹妈耶的由来。
 
Zi告诉竞核，她平时还会“潜水”在玩家QQ群里，观察大家的一举一动。TennoVIP当天凌晨5点，她就发现群里已经有了动静，自己也因为兴奋只睡了两个多小时。这种工作没有太多宏大的部分，但玩家意见与内心的真实想法正是通过这些QQ群、视频网站和线下活动进入团队视野，并进一步走进制作流程。
 
相同的逻辑也体现在内容叙事中。除了大型版本外，团队也会通过各种小任务、短片和剧情铺垫补全角色。Megan告诉我们，她在《Warframe》里最喜欢的事情之一，就是在整个《Warframe》产品里面把角色的故事给塑造好，不管是熟悉的角色还是新角色，把他们融入整个游戏的生态当中。
 
 
事实上，很多玩家愿意留下，也并非因为游戏从未出错，是因为他们相信，自己的反馈有人在听。信任也正是在一次次回应、修改和兑现中建立的。
 
这种与社区玩家建立起沟通与信任，支持玩家的价值观，在Fred看来，正是腾讯和DE合作中，双方达成的第一个、也可以说是最核心的契合点。

看见中国元素，理解中国故事
 
如果说，两场截然不同的活动体验，让我对游戏的未来充满信心；那么主创团队在交流中对中国元素，中国故事发自内心的喜爱，则让我对游戏在中国的未来充满想象。
 
过去几年里，不难发现DE对中国玩家越来越重视。
 
在游戏内容上，他们曾从中国神话中汲取灵感，推出悟空、哪吒等国风战甲；在社区沟通上，团队也开始在国内发布月度答疑、开发者互动日记等互动内容。随着腾讯与DE合作深入，中国社区的意见也有了更直接、稳定的渠道进入开发团队。
 
 
但对于“国风内容”，许多玩家的心情其实是很复杂的。
 
一方面，玩家肯定希望在游戏中能够看到更多熟悉的文化元素，不然也不会每天盼着官方透露点嫦娥的新消息，每次都询问有没有“天庭三大反骨的最后一骨——杨戬”的计划安排。但另一方面，越是在意，便越容易担心。海外团队能否真正理解中国故事？所谓的国风内容，会不会只是一次商业层面的示好？
 
特别是随着文化内容的深入，如“嫦娥”这类不是战斗角色，却拥有更多文化背景或精神的角色逐步公布后。有人期待DE的发挥，也有人担心文化理解上的偏差，最终会让内容停留在表面，甚至产生“还不如不做”的结果。
 
但此次采访则让我看到，DE并不是出于任务或者要求，而是发自内心的尝试理解和欣赏中国的文化和故事。
 
活动前，主创团队不仅参观了兵马俑，也观看了“赳赳大秦”的演出等等。Rebecca对演出中天气配合剧情变化的呈现方式赞不绝口，并希望能在游戏里也增加类似的体验。兵马俑更是她印象最深的内容，她甚至当场表示未来大家应该会看到一些灵感源于兵马俑的内容。
 
而Megan则向我们表示，她印象最深刻的是一场以武则天为主题展开的国风晚宴，他们身穿汉服边吃饭，边观看演出。无论是武则天本身的服饰，还是其背后的故事都给她带来了非常大的震撼。女皇、皇帝、兵和马等战斗元素更是给了她许多的灵感。
 
 
这种兴趣也体现在一些很小的细节里。
 
Rebecca告诉我们，她的中文老师当天也来到了活动现场。在交流过程中，她更是不断尝试用中文与我们对话。她的中文当然谈不上熟练，有时只是一句简单的问候，或者夹在英文回答中的几个词，但也正因为如此，这种略显笨拙的尝试反而显得真实。
 
此次西安之行，也让我重新理解了腾讯与DE在中国市场的合作。活动不仅面向玩家，同样也是给团队一次更好了解中国文化的机会。
 
社区梗的翻译只是第一步。当合作进一步进入内容和文化层面，只知道某个符号“很受欢迎”显然还远远不够。为此，除了参观兵马俑、观看演出，腾讯还特意邀请主要研究方向为古代神话与文学及中国艺术史的同济大学人文学院教授李晨，与DE交流传统文化，帮助他们理解嫦娥等文化形象背后的文化内涵。
 
 
在采访最后，Rebecca已经开始计划下一次中国之行。她想去重庆，也想去成都，还提前向玩家提出要求：“给我准备辣的，但Megan不要辣。”她甚至希望玩家能帮忙说服腾讯团队，把下一次访问安排在成都。
 
Megan则感谢中国玩家社区欢迎他们来到中国，让他们有机会体验和了解中国文化。Zi也请玩家继续期待接下来的内容。
 
至于说DE最终能否做好嫦娥的内容，答案仍然要留给正式内容。一次线下活动无法消除玩家对文化理解偏差的担忧，团队表现出的兴趣，也需要通过未来的作品得到验证。
 
但这次活动至少说明，《Warframe》之所以还能保持年轻，不是它知道所有正确答案。更重要的可能是，面对一个暂时无法理解的梗、一种陌生的文化，或者一个意外出现的Bug，它至今仍然愿意来到玩家身边，继续问一句：
 
为什么大家会喜欢它？

title: 同时在线13万创新高：褒贬不一的《伊莫》，怎么就畅销Top 5了？
author:
游戏葡萄
2026-09-19 17:33
+订阅
text:
口嫌体正直？
文/王丹
9月16日，上线PC和主机端的当天，由爪印工作室研发、FunPlus孵化的捉宠游戏《伊莫》，在Steam收获了约1000条评测，好评率仅有50%。
可别说什么国人玩家爱打差评……这1K条评测里，只有约100条是中文评测。仅50%好评，褒贬不一，几乎可以说是实打实老外给的分数。
那天，我已经看到有水友开始分析探讨《伊莫》的败局成因，似乎在舆论声里，它已经成了行业又一个「大烟花」。
展开剩余
88%
但今天，瞅见Steam全球畅销榜时，我有点看不懂了——上线第四天，褒贬不一的《伊莫》，仍在Steam全球畅销Top 7。
据Steam Ranks统计，9月18日，《伊莫》还曾最高冲到Steam全球畅销Top 5。 （海外和我们有时差，Steam Ranks统计的9月18日有可能对应截至国内9月19日凌晨）
据SteamDB，《伊莫》的每日同时在线人数波动也相当稳健，连续几天峰值在13W左右。北京时间9月19日凌晨1点，《伊莫》还破了自己的同在峰值纪录。照这个走势，保不准后面同在峰值最高数据还要继续刷新。
如果直接看Steam商店页，《伊莫》的评测依然显示褒贬不一，口碑似乎并未好转。但细看才能发现，《伊莫》的好评率，其实已经从第一天的50%，上升到了67%。 （Steam好评率涨到70%以上，才会变成多半好评）
难不成老外「真香」，又突然爱了？翻看《伊莫》的差评后，我发现情况比我以为的更复杂。
不喜欢一款游戏，给它打差评，然后流失走人，这是我理解的常规流程。但《伊莫》这边，有不少老外打了差评后还在接着玩。就好像，骂归骂，那和玩不玩，氪不氪是两码事。
有人玩了2小时后，怒喷《伊莫》只是套了层好看皮囊的典中典国产抽卡手游，说这是纯商人做的产品，内购商业化手段令人懊恼，末尾还加了句“Best to pass this up, no question. （最好跳过，别玩这游戏，准没错。） ”
尽管嘴上骂得毫不留情，「过去2周20.5小时」的游戏时长，却暴露了这位玩家其实没有选择跳过，而是接着继续玩，还玩了挺久……考虑到《伊莫》在Steam上最后一次测试于7月结束，「过去2周」显示的游玩时长，很大概率就是9月这波正式版上线后的游戏时长。
类似的情况还有很多，有人骂《伊莫》美术和音乐有AI味儿，有人说它是走上岔路、只想捞钱的工业垃圾……就GamesRadar等外媒报道来看，「游戏本体免费，但有体力系统、战令、便利性付费点等内购商业化设计」，确实是《伊莫》差评比较集中爆发的点。
但还是那句话，骂归骂，玩归玩，两件事不冲突。有些玩家骂得特别狠，但过去2周游戏时长却有十几甚至几十小时。
其他更多玩家的留言，与其说是打差评，不如说更像是在提反馈。
有位玩了62小时的玩家打差评，说《伊莫》做得很美，但多人模式不够好玩，恳请开发团队改改多人模式；有位玩了35小时的玩家给出差评，说这游戏是好玩的，就是UI做得太烦人了；还有位玩了近20小时的玩家直言，打差评纯粹是为了给开发团队传话，希望他们更改隐私政策里的某个条款……
结合这些留言来看，《伊莫》的内核级反作弊程序 （游戏并非以竞技为主，一些玩家认为压根没必要装这个组件，且觉得这个组件牵扯到安全和隐私问题） ，以及不够深入的多人模式、被质疑带有AI味儿的美术和音乐、UI交互、普通到略显平庸的剧情，还有被人集中吐槽的商业化设计……这些都是让老外不爽的点。
但翻了一圈差评下来，葡萄君没看到太多集中喷美术精度和玩法机制的。一些差评在提意见时，往往还会指出游戏本身机制做得不错，画面也挺精美。
反过来讲，对于那些不介意这种商业模式，也对多人模式没什么高要求的玩家来说，《伊莫》似乎没太明显的短板。
一些好评玩家直言“别被褒贬不一给骗了”。有人解释说，很多玩家看到内购就以为《伊莫》是逼氪型抽卡游戏，但实际上《伊莫》的稀有宠物可以靠自己捕捉；在游戏正式版上线前，《伊莫》还删除了Rift Exploration系统 （玩家消耗高级货币反复参与挑战，概率捕获传奇伊莫） 和符文插槽系统，现在游戏里并没有付费抽卡项目。
归根结底，《伊莫》最集中的，关于商业化设计的差评，在我看来和玩家的习惯和接受度有关。
毕竟常玩GaaS，特别是移动端GaaS游戏的玩家，就是比Steam单机爱好者，更频繁接触且更容易习惯「F2P+内购」。
有人在好评中表示，自己觉得免费游戏做内购很正常——免费游戏不也得挣钱吃饭？还有玩家在评测里拿《原神》等游戏类比，表示《伊莫》卖外观，卖战令、月卡，卖养成资源材料、改变宠物属性的道具等，都属于常规设计，谈不上激进。
不氪，这些东西玩家依旧有办法获得；付费，无非就是缩短获取过程。
从更刁钻的年龄段角度来说，新一代年轻玩家，或许也比在泡在主机、PC游戏里长大的玩家，更容易接受这样的商业模式。
看到这条评论，我想起前段时间海外游戏媒体人Rob Zacny讲过，他曾在圣诞节给侄子侄女送了一堆主机游戏，还觉得自己这叔叔当得很酷，结果到现场看侄子侄女实操后他才发现自己大错特错：“他们是真的不知道怎么玩。”和自己身边有孩子的朋友们聊过后，Rob发现，主机几乎已经是「父母辈」的娱乐项目了，很多朋友家里的小孩平常都是拿平板、手机玩游戏。
这下再回看《伊莫》50%褒贬不一的开局，以及大量关于商业化设计的差评，我觉得或许只能说明，Steam平台上较为主流的用户受众，确实不喜欢这款游戏的商业模式，我们很难因此就说它败了——这些用户打差评，一不代表他们会流失，二不代表其他泛用户的想法。
况且，《伊莫》的免费游玩，还极大降低了吃瓜群众的试错成本。买断制大作，花大几百买下来，玩了2小时后发现不喜欢，会不方便退款，所以如果游戏本身口碑不好，一些玩家会选择观望，不会直接以身入局；免费游戏就没这种负担了，反正不要钱，别人夸也好骂也好，自己总归可以试试。
当然，话说回来，我们也不能猴急地下结论说《伊莫》已经大成功。
首先，《伊莫》在Steam上线还不过一周，数据能否维持还需观察。
其次，抛开关于商业化的集中差评来看，Steam部分玩家关于UI、多人模式、剧情的不满，是真实存在的。
最后，《伊莫》将在9月23日上线移动端，届时主机、PC、移动端多平台铺开后，我们才能看到更全面的玩家反馈。
所以，还是让子弹再飞一会儿吧。

口嫌体正直？

文/王丹

9月16日，上线PC和主机端的当天，由爪印工作室研发、FunPlus孵化的捉宠游戏《伊莫》，在Steam收获了约1000条评测，好评率仅有50%。

可别说什么国人玩家爱打差评……这1K条评测里，只有约100条是中文评测。仅50%好评，褒贬不一，几乎可以说是实打实老外给的分数。

那天，我已经看到有水友开始分析探讨《伊莫》的败局成因，似乎在舆论声里，它已经成了行业又一个「大烟花」。

展开剩余
88%

但今天，瞅见Steam全球畅销榜时，我有点看不懂了——上线第四天，褒贬不一的《伊莫》，仍在Steam全球畅销Top 7。

据Steam Ranks统计，9月18日，《伊莫》还曾最高冲到Steam全球畅销Top 5。（海外和我们有时差，Steam Ranks统计的9月18日有可能对应截至国内9月19日凌晨）

据SteamDB，《伊莫》的每日同时在线人数波动也相当稳健，连续几天峰值在13W左右。北京时间9月19日凌晨1点，《伊莫》还破了自己的同在峰值纪录。照这个走势，保不准后面同在峰值最高数据还要继续刷新。

如果直接看Steam商店页，《伊莫》的评测依然显示褒贬不一，口碑似乎并未好转。但细看才能发现，《伊莫》的好评率，其实已经从第一天的50%，上升到了67%。（Steam好评率涨到70%以上，才会变成多半好评）

难不成老外「真香」，又突然爱了？翻看《伊莫》的差评后，我发现情况比我以为的更复杂。

不喜欢一款游戏，给它打差评，然后流失走人，这是我理解的常规流程。但《伊莫》这边，有不少老外打了差评后还在接着玩。就好像，骂归骂，那和玩不玩，氪不氪是两码事。

有人玩了2小时后，怒喷《伊莫》只是套了层好看皮囊的典中典国产抽卡手游，说这是纯商人做的产品，内购商业化手段令人懊恼，末尾还加了句“Best to pass this up, no question.（最好跳过，别玩这游戏，准没错。）”

尽管嘴上骂得毫不留情，「过去2周20.5小时」的游戏时长，却暴露了这位玩家其实没有选择跳过，而是接着继续玩，还玩了挺久……考虑到《伊莫》在Steam上最后一次测试于7月结束，「过去2周」显示的游玩时长，很大概率就是9月这波正式版上线后的游戏时长。

类似的情况还有很多，有人骂《伊莫》美术和音乐有AI味儿，有人说它是走上岔路、只想捞钱的工业垃圾……就GamesRadar等外媒报道来看，「游戏本体免费，但有体力系统、战令、便利性付费点等内购商业化设计」，确实是《伊莫》差评比较集中爆发的点。

但还是那句话，骂归骂，玩归玩，两件事不冲突。有些玩家骂得特别狠，但过去2周游戏时长却有十几甚至几十小时。

其他更多玩家的留言，与其说是打差评，不如说更像是在提反馈。

有位玩了62小时的玩家打差评，说《伊莫》做得很美，但多人模式不够好玩，恳请开发团队改改多人模式；有位玩了35小时的玩家给出差评，说这游戏是好玩的，就是UI做得太烦人了；还有位玩了近20小时的玩家直言，打差评纯粹是为了给开发团队传话，希望他们更改隐私政策里的某个条款……

结合这些留言来看，《伊莫》的内核级反作弊程序（游戏并非以竞技为主，一些玩家认为压根没必要装这个组件，且觉得这个组件牵扯到安全和隐私问题），以及不够深入的多人模式、被质疑带有AI味儿的美术和音乐、UI交互、普通到略显平庸的剧情，还有被人集中吐槽的商业化设计……这些都是让老外不爽的点。

但翻了一圈差评下来，葡萄君没看到太多集中喷美术精度和玩法机制的。一些差评在提意见时，往往还会指出游戏本身机制做得不错，画面也挺精美。

反过来讲，对于那些不介意这种商业模式，也对多人模式没什么高要求的玩家来说，《伊莫》似乎没太明显的短板。

一些好评玩家直言“别被褒贬不一给骗了”。有人解释说，很多玩家看到内购就以为《伊莫》是逼氪型抽卡游戏，但实际上《伊莫》的稀有宠物可以靠自己捕捉；在游戏正式版上线前，《伊莫》还删除了Rift Exploration系统（玩家消耗高级货币反复参与挑战，概率捕获传奇伊莫）和符文插槽系统，现在游戏里并没有付费抽卡项目。

归根结底，《伊莫》最集中的，关于商业化设计的差评，在我看来和玩家的习惯和接受度有关。

毕竟常玩GaaS，特别是移动端GaaS游戏的玩家，就是比Steam单机爱好者，更频繁接触且更容易习惯「F2P+内购」。

看到这条评论，我想起前段时间海外游戏媒体人Rob Zacny讲过，他曾在圣诞节给侄子侄女送了一堆主机游戏，还觉得自己这叔叔当得很酷，结果到现场看侄子侄女实操后他才发现自己大错特错：“他们是真的不知道怎么玩。”和自己身边有孩子的朋友们聊过后，Rob发现，主机几乎已经是「父母辈」的娱乐项目了，很多朋友家里的小孩平常都是拿平板、手机玩游戏。

title: 1.5 Million Copies Sold on the First Day: A New Approach for a Long-Standing IP
text:
Priced at 298 yuan, this game sold over 1.5 million copies on its release day, jumping to fifth place on the best-seller chart and firmly claiming the top spot on the wish list chart, where it remains to this day.This title, bearing the “007” name, has captured the attention of numerous players with its strong performance and has garnered over 25,000 positive reviews.In the week leading up to its release, the equally pricey *LEGO Batman* had just won over many players, and shortly thereafter, 007 once again successfully opened the wallets of the same—or a different—group of players.
If I recall correctly, the last 007-related game released was *007 Legends* in 2012. However, that title was a complete disaster both critically and commercially, and even directly led to the demise of its developer, Eurocom.This time, the task has fallen to IO Interactive, a studio renowned for its open-world stealth and assassination gameplay. Naturally, some players are comparing the new title to the studio’s classic *Hitman 47* series, trying to spot the differences.
This game largely retains some of the key elements that IOI does best, while incorporating the unique charm of 007.Compared to Agent 47—who is aloof, taciturn, and swift in action—007 has a full head of hair; he is no longer taciturn or cold-hearted, nor does he vanish into thin air after completing a mission with precision. So, just how many similarities does this game actually share with the Hitman 47 series?Faced with the challenge of creating a similar genre while still distinguishing itself, what trade-offs and choices did IOI make to better align with the classic 007 spy narrative? This game offers us plenty of insights into these questions.
01
A new suit for 007
*007: The Early Years* is a third-person spy action-adventure game that tells the story of James Bond’s early years. At this point, he had not yet become the agent we know as “007,” but was merely a naval aviator.During a secret evacuation mission, the plane he was aboard was accidentally shot down, leaving him as the sole survivor. Subsequently, MI6 recruited him into the newly launched “Agent 00 Program,” which aimed to revolutionize global intelligence operations by incorporating the “human factor.”
This narrative approach cleverly sidesteps a common pitfall in film adaptations: Should players emulate Sean Connery or Daniel Craig? Once a specific on-screen Bond becomes the benchmark, the challenge of recreating classic scenes becomes unavoidable.Instead, IOI chose to take Bond back to his roots, presenting a younger version of the character. He possesses both ability and charm, yet is not without a touch of recklessness. Not yet fully accustomed to the rules of the spy game, the flexibility and spirit of adventure he displays are precisely why MI6 chose him.
Compared to pure gameplay, this title places greater emphasis on a cinematic experience, which is clearly reflected in the pacing and presentation of the story. The game’s narrative revolves around themes such as deception and trust, artificial intelligence, and power struggles within intelligence agencies.Players will encounter scenes common to spy-themed works, such as high-speed car chases, massive explosions, intense hand-to-hand combat on airplanes, and thrilling aerial stunts, offering an adventure that balances visual spectacle with engaging gameplay.
A variety of gameplay styles coexist harmoniously in the character of 007, and IOI has executed these designs in a very natural and fluid manner. In terms of gameplay, players can choose to go stealth or engage in all-out combat; they can use a poison dart gun to make guards back off, or simply knock out enemies with their fists.
*007: A New Beginning* differs significantly from the *Hitman 47* series in terms of stealth design. While *Hitman 47*’s stealth style emphasizes meticulousness and precision, *007* takes a more forgiving approach to stealth.In *Hitman 47*, a minor mistake—such as misjudging an enemy’s patrol route or accidentally exposing yourself—can quickly escalate into an unmanageable situation, with the worst-case scenario being that all enemies turn hostile.In *007*, stealth has more of a social engineering aspect; even if 007 is spotted, he can often use clever rhetoric to convince enemies that his actions are justified.In the game, players often see 007 blending into the crowd, using his personal charm, information advantage, and appropriate disguises to turn the situation to his advantage. What’s even more interesting is that once he’s successfully persuaded an enemy, they might choose to turn a blind eye even if the player causes chaos or destruction right in front of them.
Agent 47’s stealth is more like the art of precisely manipulating the butterfly effect: by skillfully using various tools, he gradually guides enemies to change their behavior, ultimately completing the assassination with elegance. James Bond, on the other hand, offers players greater leeway; even if the process is a bit rough around the edges, they can still achieve the ultimate goal.If a mistake is made along the way and the player is spotted by enemies, they can simply go head-to-head, resolving the situation through an exhilarating fight, taking down all enemies, and then resuming stealth—without running the risk of triggering a full-scale alarm like 47 does.Therefore, by comparison, 47 is like a precise and sharp scalpel—he must handle situations with stealth, speed, and precision—while 007 is more like a Swiss Army knife, allowing players to choose more flexible and relaxed methods to complete missions.
The combat, however, is surprisingly good—perhaps thanks to the fact that its lead designer is none other than Adam Vincent, the man behind the combat mechanics in the Batman: Arkham series. He has taken the previously somewhat lackluster combat in 47 and elevated it to a much more exciting level.There are handguns, long guns, silencers, armored enemies, destructible cover, and even full-scale firefights triggered by the “License to Kill.”By combining environmental props with agent gadgets, players can pull off some incredibly stylish moves: first, use an agent gadget to destroy the environment and take out enemies, then use another to distract them, before emerging from the smoke like a specter to execute them both.This style undoubtedly aligns more closely with most players’ expectations of the 007 character—combining formidable combat skills with a sense of drama and heroism.
One thing that must be mentioned is that many players have complained that the checkpoint settings in the auto-save system are not reasonable.When a player’s character dies due to a mistake, they sometimes have to rewind to a checkpoint from much earlier in the game to start over, which has been a source of frustration for some players. If a free-save feature were added to the game, it would not only allow players to control the game’s progression at their own pace but also provide more flexibility to explore different choices and paths.
02
IOI, as a tailor
As a timeless IP, 007 has not only made a huge impact in the worlds of film and literature but has also developed a unique model of industrial collaboration over the years. For IOI, securing the 007 license is just the beginning; the real challenge lies in striking a balance between staying true to the classics and embracing innovation.If the team chooses to directly recreate movie plotlines, the execution might be highly polished, but the story would ultimately belong neither to IOI nor fully to the players. If they avoid this route, they’ll need to invest more time and effort into meticulously refining the script—though they could draw on some of Hitman 47’s narrative techniques and adapt them accordingly.In any case, every generation of 007 has its own distinctive cultural symbols. If Bond’s character had remained unchanged over time, this IP would have long since become obsolete.
From the rugged Connery Bond of the Cold War era, to the more 1990s-action-movie-style Brosnan Bond, to the Craig Bond—imbued with realism and a sense of pain, reflecting the backdrop of the war on terror—each generation of the agent has showcased a distinct personality and style.Hakan Abrak, head of IOI Studios, admitted in an interview that they have full confidence in the 007 IP: “Bond is undoubtedly one of the world’s top IPs, and it’s been over a decade since a new game based on this IP was released. For us, this is both an opportunity and a challenge…We hope this will be more than just a game; we want it to become a ‘Bond universe’ that belongs to the players.”
As mentioned earlier, IOI chose to craft an original story featuring a young Bond from the ground up. This not only successfully avoided the risk of being constrained by the image of a specific film actor but also allowed Patrick Gibson’s portrayal of Bond to develop a unique performance style, thereby preventing frame-by-frame comparisons with the film versions.Furthermore, this premise allows ample room for the game’s pacing to develop—the young Bond has not yet fully matured and does not yet have full access to his capabilities, enabling gameplay elements such as gear, combat, and rule design to unfold gradually. As the character grows, this creates a rich and sustained experience for players.Compared to a one-off film adaptation, an original story offers greater long-term development potential. This not only provides IOI with greater commercial returns but also gives the team the opportunity to delve deeper into and explore the many possibilities of the 007 character.
When players learned that IOI had secured the rights to develop a 007 game, their first reaction was naturally to anticipate a dynamic, open-world experience akin to the *Hitman* series, and to wonder what kind of sparks would fly from placing 007 within such a design framework.However, having 007 constantly change disguises and remain silent would obviously feel a bit awkward, so IOI has emphasized the large-scale spectacle elements—familiar to audiences from spy movies—as well as narrative techniques like cinematic cutscenes.
The reason many IP-based games fall short of expectations is likely that developers have not truly understood the core appeal of the IP itself; an IP is far more than just a library of assets. Characters are treated as mere entities with descriptions, while props and scenes are treated as superficial decorations. Ultimately, players are left with nothing more than a hollow shell of the IP.The key to adapting a well-established IP lies in finding a way that not only earns the trust of the rights holders but also integrates seamlessly into the game design to ensure long-term commercial sustainability.The strength of *007: A New Beginning* lies in its ability to maintain visual consistency while not being confined to the script of any single film; it makes judicious use of the core characteristics of the Bond brand to provide maximum flexibility for the game system.Cinematic storytelling helps establish Bond’s identity, while gadgets and stealth gameplay immerse players in the experience of being a secret agent. Meanwhile, close-quarters combat and interspersed action sequences showcase Bond’s unparalleled agility and flexibility. This multi-layered approach breathes new life into 007.
Items such as suits, firearms, watches, gadgets, vehicles, classic mission outfits, theme music, and Deluxe Edition bonus content all hold a certain appeal to paying players.However, this also carries a risk—while it allows players to shape their own vision of 007’s appearance and attracts attention through classic symbols, it must not come across as overly tacky.After all, Agent 007 embodies a sense of sophistication and elegance; if the in-game store becomes overrun with an overly tacky or commercialized atmosphere, it could negatively impact the player experience.
03
From Assassination Sandbox to Spy Action
There is no doubt that IOI has become highly proficient in developing the Hitman series, but this very proficiency could also become a potential hindrance.The massive success of the Hitman series stems from a highly refined game architecture: complex and ingenious level design, nuanced character profiles, realistic NPC behavior chains, diverse cover areas, environmental interaction mechanics, and an interwoven mission narrative.Through these rich systems, players observe the workings of a virtual society and then seek the optimal moment to intervene and disrupt it. This system-driven stealth mechanic has long been an unparalleled benchmark in the gaming industry.
However, when a team is long defined by its signature title, new works often struggle to escape the shadow of the past. Of course, compared to innovations in gameplay structure, technical innovations—such as the driving system, cinematic sequences, motion capture, and melee feedback—can be addressed by bringing in specialized talent, while the greater challenge lies in the process of redefining the studio’s identity.For IOI, they need to recognize that the framework of *Hitman* cannot be directly applied to the *007* project, and then consider how to innovate while maintaining their own strengths.To their credit, IOI did not simply replicate the “Bond-style 47” formula in this experiment, nor did they turn 007 into a run-of-the-mill shooter; instead, they rebalanced the emphasis on various aspects of the game.
An excessive focus on cinematic elements may dilute IOI’s strengths in sandbox depth. If the game features too many QTEs, chase sequences, and linear cutscenes, hardcore stealth players may feel they lack the freedom to play their own way. After all, in a true stealth assassination scenario, players expect the joy of discovering their own paths.Excessive dynamic cutscenes may diminish players’ sense of accomplishment. While solving problems through systematic thinking may not be as immediate or flashy as direct action sequences, an overemphasis on action can undermine the experience of autonomous decision-making provided by the system, depriving players of a unique sense of satisfaction.Furthermore, if the combat rules are not set up properly, they can actually have a negative impact. For example, if the “license to kill” triggers too easily, players may be tempted to fire their weapons frequently, neglecting more strategic approaches; conversely, if the threshold for triggering it is too high, it limits players’ freedom to experiment with various forms of combat.
This also offers insight into IOI’s thinking regarding the single-player business model. One of the challenges facing traditional linear action-adventure games is that their high development costs are difficult to justify given how quickly the content is consumed: the entire main story can be completed in just over a dozen hours, and players’ enthusiasm wanes rapidly once they finish the game.Although additional content such as DLC, deluxe editions, skins, and outfits can be sold separately, without the support of replayability, these items easily become mere garnishes alongside the main course.
Since the launch of the new *Hitman* trilogy, IOI has been exploring new avenues in replayability and system design, and the TacSim mode in this *007* title is a continuation and deepening of those efforts.While the cinematic main story aims to provide most players with an immersive James Bond movie experience, TacSim offers hardcore players who are passionate about studying game mechanics a platform to unleash their creativity and challenge themselves. Elements such as challenge modes, scoring systems, restricted conditions, leaderboards, and the unlocking of weapons and outfits are skillfully integrated into this framework.For example, completing missions using only specific items, remaining undetected, employing non-lethal tactics, or executing time-limited evacuations—or even adjusting enemy distribution and mission objectives—all allow existing scene resources to be reused multiple times without the need to remake the entire game.
Conclusion
For a veteran game studio like IOI, sticking to established formulas is clearly no longer enough to keep pace with the ever-changing market. In recent years, their traditional gameplay has increasingly failed to meet the needs of modern players, but the arrival of the 007 project has provided IOI with a new turning point.This not only provided the studio with a breakthrough but also demonstrated its ability to successfully channel years of accumulated experience into a new direction. The character of Bond, with his spirit of innovation and adventure, has also infused IOI’s titles with a fresh, contemporary vitality.
Although many players may still be hoping for IOI to release a brand-new open-world title or continue the story of Agent 47, this collaboration has demonstrated IOI’s potential in cinematic narrative games and earned widespread recognition.The legend of 007 will continue, whether or not IOI is at the helm. The question is whether IOI will be able to maintain its influence in future 007 stories—the next chapters of this classic IP—while transforming this experience into a driving force for its own growth.
In *007: No Time to Die*, the new Bond is learning how to become Agent 007, while IOI is also learning how to break free from being defined solely by the *Killer* series. This current endeavor feels more like the first step toward opening that door.Naturally, beyond that door lie more opportunities, but also more substantial challenges.

Priced at 298 yuan, this game sold over 1.5 million copies on its release day, jumping to fifth place on the best-seller chart and firmly claiming the top spot on the wish list chart, where it remains to this day.This title, bearing the “007” name, has captured the attention of numerous players with its strong performance and has garnered over 25,000 positive reviews.In the week leading up to its release, the equally pricey *LEGO Batman* had just won over many players, and shortly thereafter, 007 once again successfully opened the wallets of the same—or a different—group of players.

If I recall correctly, the last 007-related game released was *007 Legends* in 2012. However, that title was a complete disaster both critically and commercially, and even directly led to the demise of its developer, Eurocom.This time, the task has fallen to IO Interactive, a studio renowned for its open-world stealth and assassination gameplay. Naturally, some players are comparing the new title to the studio’s classic *Hitman 47* series, trying to spot the differences.

This game largely retains some of the key elements that IOI does best, while incorporating the unique charm of 007.Compared to Agent 47—who is aloof, taciturn, and swift in action—007 has a full head of hair; he is no longer taciturn or cold-hearted, nor does he vanish into thin air after completing a mission with precision. So, just how many similarities does this game actually share with the Hitman 47 series?Faced with the challenge of creating a similar genre while still distinguishing itself, what trade-offs and choices did IOI make to better align with the classic 007 spy narrative? This game offers us plenty of insights into these questions.

01

A new suit for 007

*007: The Early Years* is a third-person spy action-adventure game that tells the story of James Bond’s early years. At this point, he had not yet become the agent we know as “007,” but was merely a naval aviator.During a secret evacuation mission, the plane he was aboard was accidentally shot down, leaving him as the sole survivor. Subsequently, MI6 recruited him into the newly launched “Agent 00 Program,” which aimed to revolutionize global intelligence operations by incorporating the “human factor.”

This narrative approach cleverly sidesteps a common pitfall in film adaptations: Should players emulate Sean Connery or Daniel Craig? Once a specific on-screen Bond becomes the benchmark, the challenge of recreating classic scenes becomes unavoidable.Instead, IOI chose to take Bond back to his roots, presenting a younger version of the character. He possesses both ability and charm, yet is not without a touch of recklessness. Not yet fully accustomed to the rules of the spy game, the flexibility and spirit of adventure he displays are precisely why MI6 chose him.

Compared to pure gameplay, this title places greater emphasis on a cinematic experience, which is clearly reflected in the pacing and presentation of the story. The game’s narrative revolves around themes such as deception and trust, artificial intelligence, and power struggles within intelligence agencies.Players will encounter scenes common to spy-themed works, such as high-speed car chases, massive explosions, intense hand-to-hand combat on airplanes, and thrilling aerial stunts, offering an adventure that balances visual spectacle with engaging gameplay.

A variety of gameplay styles coexist harmoniously in the character of 007, and IOI has executed these designs in a very natural and fluid manner. In terms of gameplay, players can choose to go stealth or engage in all-out combat; they can use a poison dart gun to make guards back off, or simply knock out enemies with their fists.

*007: A New Beginning* differs significantly from the *Hitman 47* series in terms of stealth design. While *Hitman 47*’s stealth style emphasizes meticulousness and precision, *007* takes a more forgiving approach to stealth.In *Hitman 47*, a minor mistake—such as misjudging an enemy’s patrol route or accidentally exposing yourself—can quickly escalate into an unmanageable situation, with the worst-case scenario being that all enemies turn hostile.In *007*, stealth has more of a social engineering aspect; even if 007 is spotted, he can often use clever rhetoric to convince enemies that his actions are justified.In the game, players often see 007 blending into the crowd, using his personal charm, information advantage, and appropriate disguises to turn the situation to his advantage. What’s even more interesting is that once he’s successfully persuaded an enemy, they might choose to turn a blind eye even if the player causes chaos or destruction right in front of them.

Agent 47’s stealth is more like the art of precisely manipulating the butterfly effect: by skillfully using various tools, he gradually guides enemies to change their behavior, ultimately completing the assassination with elegance. The combat, however, is surprisingly good—perhaps thanks to the fact that its lead designer is none other than Adam Vincent, the man behind the combat mechanics in the Batman: Arkham series. One thing that must be mentioned is that many players have complained that the checkpoint settings in the auto-save system are not reasonable.When a player’s character dies due to a mistake, they sometimes have to rewind to a checkpoint from much earlier in the game to start over, which has been a source of frustration for some players. If a free-save feature were added to the game, it would not only allow players to control the game’s progression at their own pace but also provide more flexibility to explore different choices and paths.

02

IOI, as a tailor

As a timeless IP, 007 has not only made a huge impact in the worlds of film and literature but has also developed a unique model of industrial collaboration over the years. For IOI, securing the 007 license is just the beginning; the real challenge lies in striking a balance between staying true to the classics and embracing innovation.If the team chooses to directly recreate movie plotlines, the execution might be highly polished, but the story would ultimately belong neither to IOI nor fully to the players. If they avoid this route, they’ll need to invest more time and effort into meticulously refining the script—though they could draw on some of Hitman 47’s narrative techniques and adapt them accordingly.In any case, every generation of 007 has its own distinctive cultural symbols. If Bond’s character had remained unchanged over time, this IP would have long since become obsolete.

From the rugged Connery Bond of the Cold War era, to the more 1990s-action-movie-style Brosnan Bond, to the Craig Bond—imbued with realism and a sense of pain, reflecting the backdrop of the war on terror—each generation of the agent has showcased a distinct personality and style.Hakan Abrak, head of IOI Studios, admitted in an interview that they have full confidence in the 007 IP: “Bond is undoubtedly one of the world’s top IPs, and it’s been over a decade since a new game based on this IP was released. For us, this is both an opportunity and a challenge…We hope this will be more than just a game; we want it to become a ‘Bond universe’ that belongs to the players.”

As mentioned earlier, IOI chose to craft an original story featuring a young Bond from the ground up. This not only successfully avoided the risk of being constrained by the image of a specific film actor but also allowed Patrick Gibson’s portrayal of Bond to develop a unique performance style, thereby preventing frame-by-frame comparisons with the film versions.Furthermore, this premise allows ample room for the game’s pacing to develop—the young Bond has not yet fully matured and does not yet have full access to his capabilities, enabling gameplay elements such as gear, combat, and rule design to unfold gradually. As the character grows, this creates a rich and sustained experience for players.Compared to a one-off film adaptation, an original story offers greater long-term development potential. This not only provides IOI with greater commercial returns but also gives the team the opportunity to delve deeper into and explore the many possibilities of the 007 character.

When players learned that IOI had secured the rights to develop a 007 game, their first reaction was naturally to anticipate a dynamic, open-world experience akin to the *Hitman* series, and to wonder what kind of sparks would fly from placing 007 within such a design framework.However, having 007 constantly change disguises and remain silent would obviously feel a bit awkward, so IOI has emphasized the large-scale spectacle elements—familiar to audiences from spy movies—as well as narrative techniques like cinematic cutscenes.

The reason many IP-based games fall short of expectations is likely that developers have not truly understood the core appeal of the IP itself; an IP is far more than just a library of assets. Characters are treated as mere entities with descriptions, while props and scenes are treated as superficial decorations. Ultimately, players are left with nothing more than a hollow shell of the IP.The key to adapting a well-established IP lies in finding a way that not only earns the trust of the rights holders but also integrates seamlessly into the game design to ensure long-term commercial sustainability.The strength of *007: A New Beginning* lies in its ability to maintain visual consistency while not being confined to the script of any single film; it makes judicious use of the core characteristics of the Bond brand to provide maximum flexibility for the game system.Cinematic storytelling helps establish Bond’s identity, while gadgets and stealth gameplay immerse players in the experience of being a secret agent. Meanwhile, close-quarters combat and interspersed action sequences showcase Bond’s unparalleled agility and flexibility. This multi-layered approach breathes new life into 007.

Items such as suits, firearms, watches, gadgets, vehicles, classic mission outfits, theme music, and Deluxe Edition bonus content all hold a certain appeal to paying players.However, this also carries a risk—while it allows players to shape their own vision of 007’s appearance and attracts attention through classic symbols, it must not come across as overly tacky.After all, Agent 007 embodies a sense of sophistication and elegance; if the in-game store becomes overrun with an overly tacky or commercialized atmosphere, it could negatively impact the player experience.

From Assassination Sandbox to Spy Action

There is no doubt that IOI has become highly proficient in developing the Hitman series, but this very proficiency could also become a potential hindrance.The massive success of the Hitman series stems from a highly refined game architecture: complex and ingenious level design, nuanced character profiles, realistic NPC behavior chains, diverse cover areas, environmental interaction mechanics, and an interwoven mission narrative.Through these rich systems, players observe the workings of a virtual society and then seek the optimal moment to intervene and disrupt it. title: In an era when major titles are being churned out like hotcakes, is NetEase launching an aircraft carrier?
text:
In 2026, the Chinese gaming industry will be both a paradise and a hell.
From a gamer’s perspective, this year is a rare bonanza for gaming: the release schedule is packed with dozens of major titles from top studios, all waiting to be explored by players, with excitement and anticipation at an all-time high.But for developers, every genre—from monster-catching to open-world to shooters—has become a cutthroat battleground. After all, each company is fielding products they’ve poured their heart and soul into, betting their future on them. In the past, high-quality visuals alone were often enough to attract attention; but this year, everyone has to pull out all the stops just to grab a slice of the limited market pie.
In this environment where everyone is under pressure, it becomes all the more clear who truly possesses the “hard power” to stand out. Take NetEase’s *Sea of Forgetfulness*, for example—in just a few days, on May 28, they will launch their third closed beta, the “Dawn” test.
Since officially obtaining their publishing license in late April, they have been working feverishly to prepare for a series of closed beta tests, with every step attracting massive spontaneous attention from players.Late last month, they released a recruitment PV for the beta test, which surpassed 6 million views on Bilibili within just a few days. At NetEase Games’ 520 launch event, many described it as the most memorable product of the day. During the subsequent preview livestream, they unveiled the game’s core mechanics and the latest developments in monetization, drawing over a million viewers shortly after the broadcast began.
Looking beyond the event, *The Forgotten Sea* has already climbed to the top of the pre-registration charts on multiple platforms, including TapTap and Bilibili, garnering over 23 million pre-registrations across the web.Players lining up in the comments section of the official account to request access or urge the launch of the open beta—these phenomena and figures send a clear signal: in an era where new games are launching in droves, *The Forgotten Sea* stands out as the most prominent titan among them, with players collectively holding high expectations for its gameplay, presentation, and every other aspect.
I, too, was among those captivated by the game. After experiencing the first two betas, I felt that *Sea of Forgetfulness* clearly had the makings of a hit: it boasts a wealth of high-quality 3D content while maintaining its own unique stylistic flair; its open-world framework—a blend of land and sea adventures woven together through a roguelike loop—is truly one-of-a-kind in the global gaming industry.During the preview livestream for the third beta, they unveiled a radically overhauled gacha monetization model. In an era where open-world games are highly homogenized, they’ve achieved a rare level of differentiation, raising our expectations for quality and content and making us optimistic about its future potential.
It’s clear—this time, NetEase is out to shake up the entire open-world gaming market.
01
More than just a polygon warrior
Taking a closer look at the discussions surrounding the third closed beta test for *The Sea of Forgetfulness*, players expressing anticipation for the game on social media can generally be divided into two categories.
One group consists of players drawn to the game’s art style—the entire set of bizarre, puppet-inspired visuals, paired with a lively, slightly tipsy vibe, is sure to appeal to the masses. The other group comprises veteran players who participated in the first two betas; they can recite the Princess’s skill lines off the top of their heads, know every nook and cranny of Otopia City, and have their own ideas about how the game could be improved for the third beta.
The latter group of players is particularly worth mentioning. Given the limited player base in both test phases and the relatively small overall user base, the game has still managed to retain a loyal core player base, demonstrating that the core experience of this treasure-hunting adventure is quite solid.
During the second beta test, Tea House also analyzed what makes *Sea of Forgetfulness* so enjoyable. It possesses a rare sense of coherence: when you launch the game, you truly feel like a Jack Sparrow-style captain, a part of this mysterious and wondrous fictional world, exploring the deepest secrets of the Sea of Forgetfulness.
At the game’s outset, you find yourself rescued from the Sea of Oblivion and brought to the small town of Otopia. Though you’ve lost all memory of your past, that doesn’t dampen your spirits: in this coastal town, you help neighbors catch chickens, compete in drinking contests with the local gang boss, and build relationships with the town’s eccentric residents, soaking up the lively atmosphere amidst all the chaos.This sense of immersion is underpinned by a massive amount of content. There are over a hundred mini-games you can play against NPCs, and some—such as mahjong and goose chess—can even be played online with other players, ensuring an experience that never gets boring.
Once you’ve rested up in Otopia, you can set sail on an expedition called “The Journey of Oblivion.” The new content officially announced during the preview livestream further clarifies the game’s central theme of “oblivion”: according to the livestream, “the ultimate destination of memory is oblivion; forgotten memories sink to the ocean floor and converge in the Sea of Oblivion.”On your voyages, you can salvage fragments of memories lost by others, and the companions behind these memories will join your party as playable characters, gradually expanding your fleet.
It’s clear, then, that this game’s core appeal lies in its replayability across multiple playthroughs—each voyage is a massive roguelike adventure set across 256 square kilometers of ocean.This world features a complex marine ecosystem and various island types, including the main island, outlying islands, and scattered islets. By battling the powerful rulers lurking throughout the world and collecting the resources and items they drop, you can enhance your team’s strength for this expedition.
A complete journey through Oblivion consists of several key stages: setting sail again with your companions, growing stronger through roguelike combat, defeating the final boss of the second beta—the mermaid Morian—and then entering the Great Tower of Memories. Once you’ve completed the “Superficial Dreams” trial, you’ll gain access to the Sea of Oblivion to retrieve your memories.
How you proceed from there is entirely up to you. In the second beta alone, there are over twenty bosses of various sizes scattered across the islands and the open sea, most of which are optional and have no set order.However, each boss drops different key class-change items and weapons, and these drops introduce random variability in skill selection, class choices, and equipment stats—thereby making the game’s roguelike loop quite distinct: depending on your playstyle, the game can spawn a wide variety of gear-building strategies.
For example, you can choose to level up steadily, experiment to discover dark cultivation strategies, or compete with other players to see who can complete the game fastest at a low level. These choices ensure that every “Journey of Oblivion” feels different from the last, keeping the experience fresh. Plus, you’re in complete control of the pace of your exploration—even when you don’t feel like fighting, you can choose to take in the scenery, hunt for treasure chests, or advance the story on the safe main island. The game’s replayability is exceptionally well-designed.
Teahouse Jun has noticed that some people have drawn parallels between the gameplay of *Journey into Oblivion* and *Elden Ring*, and it’s actually quite apt.The two games share many similarities: open-world exploration, no fixed order for boss battles, and different challenge routes leading to varied builds and outcomes. This experience, which grants players a high degree of autonomy, has led many players to complete *Elden Ring* a dozen or more times. This opens up a wealth of possibilities for *Sea of Forgetfulness*’s long-term replayability.
The difference is that, according to estimates provided during this preview livestream, a single playthrough of *Sea of Forgetfulness* averages around 3 hours, and skilled players can complete it in as little as 1.5 hours, making the time commitment more manageable compared to large-scale single-player games.Even more noteworthy is an official announcement from the development team: completing the “Journey of Oblivion” will grant players a free in-game crew member of the highest tier (equivalent to SSR) or a “Shadow of the Past.” Additionally, once a week, players have a 50% chance to obtain a Black Ticket or Purple Ticket crew member (equivalent to SR) or a “Shadow of the Past” (a crucial cultivation item).
In other words, in a game where “character gacha” serves as one of its monetization strategies, *The Forgotten Sea* doesn’t just rely on gameplay mechanics to encourage repeat play; it also positions character merchandise as the “ultimate prize” within the game’s main loop, using high drop rates to incentivize players to repeatedly engage in this “forget-remember” cycle.
This is clearly a rather bold move that has attracted significant industry attention.
02
Carving out a path through long-term operations
The introduction of the “Black Card” design sends a clear signal. It indicates that the *Sea of Forgetfulness* development team has keenly identified the issues that are gradually coming to light with the current gacha monetization model. At a time when most open-world games still treat gacha as the “standard solution,” *Sea of Forgetfulness* is resolutely challenging this industry convention while presenting a viable alternative.
Several commercialization strategists from major game studios have shared with us the view that “unlucky gacha results are good for long-term retention”: During a game’s open beta, all server launch bonuses are maxed out; players aren’t short on resources, and gacha mechanics—which offer the thrill of a blind box—can still provide a positive experience.However, after playing through a few major updates, players inevitably return to the grind of daily life. When they painstakingly save up gacha resources only to miss the guaranteed drop, the negative feedback is intense. Even if they do draw a limited-edition character, they must engage in a game of suspicion and speculation with the developers, “gambling” on whether there will still be a viable role for that character in the future. Over time, this erodes player loyalty and undermines the game’s long-term viability.
The designers of *The Sea of Forgetfulness* made it very clear during the preview livestream: in their design, the game’s monetization will primarily come from cosmetic items, such as character outfits and accessories, and the decision to purchase these items will largely be up to the players.
With cosmetic purchases providing the necessary commercial support, character acquisition can be made much more accessible.According to the project team’s vision, success in the trials of the Forgotten Journey relies primarily on leveraging roguelike mechanics to build effective decks, with powerful crew members merely serving to slightly increase the margin for error. In this test, even when drawing crew members from the gacha pool, the guaranteed reward is triggered after a maximum of 80 pulls, and the first guaranteed reward in each pool is always the featured black-ticket crew member—making the first small guaranteed reward a reality.
Combining gacha mechanics with the core gameplay of roguelike games is a particularly clever move. It ties high-value goals to the incremental objectives within the core loop. While this sacrifices some monetization potential, it addresses the more critical long-term question of “why play?” It also provides players with a psychological buffer regarding the gacha system.
Not only that, but the development team has turned these promises into reality: all Black Ticket characters and Shadows of the Past can be obtained through the Journey of Oblivion, with a guaranteed drop of a Black Ticket character or a Shadow of the Past within a maximum of three weeks. So, as long as you put in the time, you’re sure to eventually add your favorite character to your roster.

Whether in terms of pre-registrations or player engagement on social media, the numbers generated by the third closed beta test for *Sea of Forgetfulness* clearly indicate that it is highly likely to become the next game to shake up the open-world genre.
According to NetEase’s Q1 earnings report, *Sea of Forgetfulness* is expected to launch officially in the third quarter of this year—and the global open-world gaming market is bound to face fierce competition in the second half of the year.

In 2026, the Chinese gaming industry will be both a paradise and a hell.

From a gamer’s perspective, this year is a rare bonanza for gaming: the release schedule is packed with dozens of major titles from top studios, all waiting to be explored by players, with excitement and anticipation at an all-time high.But for developers, every genre—from monster-catching to open-world to shooters—has become a cutthroat battleground. After all, each company is fielding products they’ve poured their heart and soul into, betting their future on them. In the past, high-quality visuals alone were often enough to attract attention; but this year, everyone has to pull out all the stops just to grab a slice of the limited market pie.

In this environment where everyone is under pressure, it becomes all the more clear who truly possesses the “hard power” to stand out. Take NetEase’s *Sea of Forgetfulness*, for example—in just a few days, on May 28, they will launch their third closed beta, the “Dawn” test.

Since officially obtaining their publishing license in late April, they have been working feverishly to prepare for a series of closed beta tests, with every step attracting massive spontaneous attention from players.Late last month, they released a recruitment PV for the beta test, which surpassed 6 million views on Bilibili within just a few days. At NetEase Games’ 520 launch event, many described it as the most memorable product of the day. During the subsequent preview livestream, they unveiled the game’s core mechanics and the latest developments in monetization, drawing over a million viewers shortly after the broadcast began.

Looking beyond the event, *The Forgotten Sea* has already climbed to the top of the pre-registration charts on multiple platforms, including TapTap and Bilibili, garnering over 23 million pre-registrations across the web.Players lining up in the comments section of the official account to request access or urge the launch of the open beta—these phenomena and figures send a clear signal: in an era where new games are launching in droves, *The Forgotten Sea* stands out as the most prominent titan among them, with players collectively holding high expectations for its gameplay, presentation, and every other aspect.

I, too, was among those captivated by the game. After experiencing the first two betas, I felt that *Sea of Forgetfulness* clearly had the makings of a hit: it boasts a wealth of high-quality 3D content while maintaining its own unique stylistic flair; its open-world framework—a blend of land and sea adventures woven together through a roguelike loop—is truly one-of-a-kind in the global gaming industry.During the preview livestream for the third beta, they unveiled a radically overhauled gacha monetization model. In an era where open-world games are highly homogenized, they’ve achieved a rare level of differentiation, raising our expectations for quality and content and making us optimistic about its future potential.

It’s clear—this time, NetEase is out to shake up the entire open-world gaming market.

01

More than just a polygon warrior

Taking a closer look at the discussions surrounding the third closed beta test for *The Sea of Forgetfulness*, players expressing anticipation for the game on social media can generally be divided into two categories.

One group consists of players drawn to the game’s art style—the entire set of bizarre, puppet-inspired visuals, paired with a lively, slightly tipsy vibe, is sure to appeal to the masses. The other group comprises veteran players who participated in the first two betas; they can recite the Princess’s skill lines off the top of their heads, know every nook and cranny of Otopia City, and have their own ideas about how the game could be improved for the third beta.

The latter group of players is particularly worth mentioning. Given the limited player base in both test phases and the relatively small overall user base, the game has still managed to retain a loyal core player base, demonstrating that the core experience of this treasure-hunting adventure is quite solid.

During the second beta test, Tea House also analyzed what makes *Sea of Forgetfulness* so enjoyable. It possesses a rare sense of coherence: when you launch the game, you truly feel like a Jack Sparrow-style captain, a part of this mysterious and wondrous fictional world, exploring the deepest secrets of the Sea of Forgetfulness.

At the game’s outset, you find yourself rescued from the Sea of Oblivion and brought to the small town of Otopia. Though you’ve lost all memory of your past, that doesn’t dampen your spirits: in this coastal town, you help neighbors catch chickens, compete in drinking contests with the local gang boss, and build relationships with the town’s eccentric residents, soaking up the lively atmosphere amidst all the chaos.This sense of immersion is underpinned by a massive amount of content. There are over a hundred mini-games you can play against NPCs, and some—such as mahjong and goose chess—can even be played online with other players, ensuring an experience that never gets boring.

Once you’ve rested up in Otopia, you can set sail on an expedition called “The Journey of Oblivion.” The new content officially announced during the preview livestream further clarifies the game’s central theme of “oblivion”: according to the livestream, “the ultimate destination of memory is oblivion; forgotten memories sink to the ocean floor and converge in the Sea of Oblivion.”On your voyages, you can salvage fragments of memories lost by others, and the companions behind these memories will join your party as playable characters, gradually expanding your fleet.

It’s clear, then, that this game’s core appeal lies in its replayability across multiple playthroughs—each voyage is a massive roguelike adventure set across 256 square kilometers of ocean.This world features a complex marine ecosystem and various island types, including the main island, outlying islands, and scattered islets. By battling the powerful rulers lurking throughout the world and collecting the resources and items they drop, you can enhance your team’s strength for this expedition.

A complete journey through Oblivion consists of several key stages: setting sail again with your companions, growing stronger through roguelike combat, defeating the final boss of the second beta—the mermaid Morian—and then entering the Great Tower of Memories. Once you’ve completed the “Superficial Dreams” trial, you’ll gain access to the Sea of Oblivion to retrieve your memories.

How you proceed from there is entirely up to you. In the second beta alone, there are over twenty bosses of various sizes scattered across the islands and the open sea, most of which are optional and have no set order.However, each boss drops different key class-change items and weapons, and these drops introduce random variability in skill selection, class choices, and equipment stats—thereby making the game’s roguelike loop quite distinct: depending on your playstyle, the game can spawn a wide variety of gear-building strategies.

For example, you can choose to level up steadily, experiment to discover dark cultivation strategies, or compete with other players to see who can complete the game fastest at a low level. These choices ensure that every “Journey of Oblivion” feels different from the last, keeping the experience fresh. Plus, you’re in complete control of the pace of your exploration—even when you don’t feel like fighting, you can choose to take in the scenery, hunt for treasure chests, or advance the story on the safe main island. The game’s replayability is exceptionally well-designed.

Teahouse Jun has noticed that some people have drawn parallels between the gameplay of *Journey into Oblivion* and *Elden Ring*, and it’s actually quite apt.The two games share many similarities: open-world exploration, no fixed order for boss battles, and different challenge routes leading to varied builds and outcomes. This experience, which grants players a high degree of autonomy, has led many players to complete *Elden Ring* a dozen or more times. This opens up a wealth of possibilities for *Sea of Forgetfulness*’s long-term replayability.

The difference is that, according to estimates provided during this preview livestream, a single playthrough of *Sea of Forgetfulness* averages around 3 hours, and skilled players can complete it in as little as 1.5 hours, making the time commitment more manageable compared to large-scale single-player games.Even more noteworthy is an official announcement from the development team: completing the “Journey of Oblivion” will grant players a free in-game crew member of the highest tier (equivalent to SSR) or a “Shadow of the Past.” Additionally, once a week, players have a 50% chance to obtain a Black Ticket or Purple Ticket crew member (equivalent to SR) or a “Shadow of the Past” (a crucial cultivation item).

In other words, in a game where “character gacha” serves as one of its monetization strategies, *The Forgotten Sea* doesn’t just rely on gameplay mechanics to encourage repeat play; it also positions character merchandise as the “ultimate prize” within the game’s main loop, using high drop rates to incentivize players to repeatedly engage in this “forget-remember” cycle.

This is clearly a rather bold move that has attracted significant industry attention.

02

Carving out a path through long-term operations

The introduction of the “Black Card” design sends a clear signal. It indicates that the *Sea of Forgetfulness* development team has keenly identified the issues that are gradually coming to light with the current gacha monetization model. At a time when most open-world games still treat gacha as the “standard solution,” *Sea of Forgetfulness* is resolutely challenging this industry convention while presenting a viable alternative.

Several commercialization strategists from major game studios have shared with us the view that “unlucky gacha results are good for long-term retention”: During a game’s open beta, all server launch bonuses are maxed out; players aren’t short on resources, and gacha mechanics—which offer the thrill of a blind box—can still provide a positive experience.However, after playing through a few major updates, players inevitably return to the grind of daily life. When they painstakingly save up gacha resources only to miss the guaranteed drop, the negative feedback is intense. Even if they do draw a limited-edition character, they must engage in a game of suspicion and speculation with the developers, “gambling” on whether there will still be a viable role for that character in the future. Over time, this erodes player loyalty and undermines the game’s long-term viability.

The designers of *The Sea of Forgetfulness* made it very clear during the preview livestream: in their design, the game’s monetization will primarily come from cosmetic items, such as character outfits and accessories, and the decision to purchase these items will largely be up to the players.

With cosmetic purchases providing the necessary commercial support, character acquisition can be made much more accessible.According to the project team’s vision, success in the trials of the Forgotten Journey relies primarily on leveraging roguelike mechanics to build effective decks, with powerful crew members merely serving to slightly increase the margin for error. Combining gacha mechanics with the core gameplay of roguelike games is a particularly clever move. It ties high-value goals to the incremental objectives within the core loop. title: Shalu, a "dedicated community member" in the indie gaming scene, is racing against leukemia
text:
In July 2026, independent game developer Sha Lu had just completed her sixth round of chemotherapy and was still facing a 25% mortality rate.
He had been ill for a year. A year earlier, in July 2025, Sha Lu traveled to Beijing to attend the Nuclear Fusion Game Expo.During the expo, he felt weak, but he never even considered the possibility of a serious illness. Looking back, he only belatedly realized how dangerous the situation had been at the time; if he had been jostled in the crowded venue of the Beijing Nuclear Fusion Expo, “he would very likely have died on the spot.”
After the trade show was over, Sha Lu went to the hospital, where the doctor immediately admitted him; he was subsequently diagnosed with acute leukemia.
In the early stages of his illness, his condition deteriorated very rapidly. At one point, Sha Lu fell into a semi-comatose state that lasted for a month. “I had to lie in bed for more than 18 hours a day and could barely stay awake,” he said. During that month or so, he completely lost the ability to care for himself, had no time to attend to the company’s future arrangements, and even experienced two life-threatening episodes.
After his health improved slightly and he regained his ability to care for himself, Sha Lu returned to game development. He identifies as an ENTJ and believes he has a trait that makes it impossible for him to stop working: “Watching TikTok or short videos, or playing games, doesn’t necessarily bring me much joy—it’s work that brings me joy.””
01
Selling a House to Start a Business
In 1986, Sha Lu was born in Suzhou, Jiangsu. Growing up in a family of moderate means, he had access to high-quality single-player video games from an early age, such as *Phantom Sword of the Ghost City* and *The Knights of the Flame Dragon*, developed by Han Tang Studio in Taiwan, as well as *The Legend of Jin Yong’s Heroes*,*Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, and *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*.
These role-playing games had a profound influence on his aesthetic sense of gaming art. After entering high school, Shalu and several friends created accounts on Youxian.com and served as moderators for *The Age of Discovery*.He was responsible for editing game information and walkthroughs on the forum, which led him to study a great deal of geography. During a history class one day, Shalu gave a presentation to the entire class on the Age of Discovery and even earned praise from his history teacher.
After that, Sha Lu developed a keen interest in the cultural impact of video games and published an article in the school newspaper declaring that video games are the ninth art.
During his college years, this gaming enthusiast began transitioning into an indie game developer, running a gaming forum and dabbling in fan game production. Whenever he had a new idea, he would post recruitment notices on the forum to find artists, scriptwriters, and voice actors.Since fan game projects were developed on a volunteer basis—with members working purely out of interest—the teams were extremely unstable, and people would drop out every other day. Looking back on that experience, Sha Lu reflected, “A group that runs purely on passion is highly unlikely to make it to the end.”
When he first left college, he worked in other industries as well. He took 20,000 yuan from his parents as startup capital to launch his own business, selling clothing and anime merchandise, and he also capitalized on the e-commerce boom by opening a Taobao store.It was a boom period for the textile and apparel industry. Sha Lu would often ride his bicycle several kilometers to work. In the summer, when temperatures soared to over 30 degrees, he would sort through merchandise in stuffy warehouses, often ending up completely drenched in sweat.
Shalu’s autograph from the event
Although his body was exhausted, the positive feedback from the business kept coming in.Sha Lu said that compared to making games, this entrepreneurial journey didn’t feel particularly difficult. During this time, he met his current wife through the online game *Ragnarok*. The two formed a team and chatted in the game, gradually growing closer, and solidified their relationship after meeting in person at ChinaJoy in Shanghai.
The idea of making games began to stir within me once again. My wife is skilled at drawing, and Shalu handled the game design; together, the two of them spent six or seven years creating small text-adventure games.
It was August 2, 2018, and the sun was beating down on Shanghai’s Pudong district. At the bustling ChinaJoy venue in the International Exhibition Center, 32-year-old Sha Lu was chatting with a group of online friends in their twenties around a dining table when he announced to everyone that he would be closing his Taobao store—which he had run for many years—and switching careers to develop indie games.
Later, Sha Lu wrote in her blog: “I sold my house to raise money for game development. Unlike some big shots who own stacks of properties—selling one leaves them with ten more.”
02
Lose Everything
“The Ballad of the Knight,” a project launched in 2018, was the first harsh trial of Sha Lu’s career as an indie game developer.
Through a friend’s introduction, Shalu met a technical expert. At the start of the project, the team’s cost estimate was only half of what it ultimately turned out to be. However, the collaboration soon revealed problems: there was a lack of trust between the two parties, and communication was extremely difficult. In Shalu’s words, “It was like having Fan Bingbing as the ideal, Qiao Biluo as the bottom line, and an ET alien as reality.”
This technician lacked enthusiasm for developing single-player games. He repeatedly demanded that Shalu add an in-game store system, and he was also slacking off—often refusing to write code and skipping work for an entire day at a time. Shalu felt quite helpless about this: “He said he’d work at most two hours a day; if it went beyond two hours, he wouldn’t work because his efficiency would drop.He just sat there playing games all day.”
Since there were no game designers on the team, Sha Lu handled all the game design work single-handedly at the time. However, after he finished the design, the programmer told him he couldn’t understand it and demanded that Sha Lu figure it out on his own and redo it in a specified format; even the slightest deviation from the format would earn him a harsh scolding.Shalu had no choice but to push himself to the limit: “I could only sleep about four hours a day, six hours on weekends, and I handled everything else all by myself.”
Even so, he didn’t switch lead programmers midway through the project. After all, changing the lead programmer halfway through game development would mean scrapping all the code and starting the game from scratch—the sunk costs would be too high.
After months of restructuring and delays, *The Way of the Hero: A Wanderer’s Song* finally launched on September 21, 2020.At that time, Shalu was facing the dire situation of its account funds running dry; without a launch, the company would not survive, so it had no choice but to brave the competition against *Xuanyuan Sword*, released in October, and *Cyberpunk 2077*, released in November.
The current Steam homepage for “The Way of the Knight”
After the game was released, it briefly shot to the top of the New Releases and Region-Wide Best-Sellers charts. Just as Sha Lu was about to celebrate in the QQ group, a flood of negative reviews came pouring in, and the positive rating plummeted to 54%.According to Steam’s policies, games with an approval rating below 70% are demoted, and *The Way of the Knight* was immediately removed from the platform’s recommendations.
The main reasons for the negative reviews were motion sickness caused by the camera work and a save file bug. Although the Shalu team had conducted four rounds of testing and five rounds of revisions, to avoid spoilers, they limited the testers to a few trusted friends. The small sample size meant they failed to detect these critical issues.Faced with the negative reviews, the team was on pins and needles. One girl, unable to bear the pressure, retreated to the common lounge to cry. Shalu and the team released two updates in quick succession that afternoon to address the issues, and the approval rating painstakingly climbed back to 70% by 1:00 a.m.
“This time, I really experienced the thrill of a roller coaster like never before,” said Sha Lu, still shaken six years later as she revisited the topic. The game, into which she had poured her heart and soul, ultimately ended in a disastrous failure. “It was a total loss—we didn’t even recoup half of the costs.”
03
The Versatile Solo Traveler
Following the failure of *The Way of the Knight*, Sha Lu decided to start work on a new project. As a loyal fan of Atlus, he initially wanted to create a surgical simulation game similar to the Nintendo DS title *Super Surgeon*, in which a surgeon protagonist would unravel the unsolved mysteries from the previous game.After consulting industry insiders, however, he was warned that the game’s content might face censorship due to its graphic violence, so they were forced to abandon that idea and explore a new direction.
However, halfway through development of the new project, Shalu discovered that its gameplay closely resembled that of the popular game *Loop Heroes*. To avoid being accused of plagiarism by players, they had no choice but to ruthlessly scrap the half-finished project.
Subsequently, the outbreak of the pandemic brought game development to a standstill, and the team’s finances grew increasingly tight.Shalu drew inspiration from playing *13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim*, borrowing its framework of unlocking the story as the player progresses to establish the narrative structure for her new game. Titled *Floating Life: A Song of Wandering*, the game underwent numerous rewrites and revisions, taking nearly eight years to finally see the light of day.
In the first month after the game’s release, it had 800 wishlist entries—which, in Shalu’s view, was “barely passing.”Sha Lu summed up this experience in a single sentence: “I’ve always felt that making indie games is like playing the lottery.” He joked that after all these years of hard work, he had “gone from a greenhorn to an old, jaded greenhorn.”
During his eight years in the industry, in addition to R&D, Sha Lu has also handled game publishing and PR.In this regard, he is quite experienced; he helped *Death’s Rampage: The End of the Road* achieve strong sales of 100,000 copies in its first week, and he even engaged in preliminary negotiations for a blockbuster game—though unfortunately, the partnership ultimately fell through due to internal factional disputes within the company. Even at the time of this interview, he still expressed regret over the situation.
Sha Lu Attended the China Game Developers Conference and Delivered a Speech

Furthermore, based on his own experience handling publishing and PR, Sha Lu believes that good publishing involves more than just buying video ads; it also requires helping developers with testing, optimization, and providing localization advice—a complex and time-consuming process.
