04
Concerned Citizen
An indie game developer had this to say about Sha Lu: “It’s hard to find an indie game developer who doesn’t know him. You see him in all kinds of groups—Sha Lu comes across as a caring community member.”
To date, Shalu has helped indie developers release five single-player and board game titles free of charge, and has also organized numerous charitable activities within the indie gaming community. For example, during the 2021 pandemic, Shalu noticed a strong demand for partners in various developer groups and consequently created a shared document where indie game developers could post requests to form teams.

Later, because it infringed on the interests of certain individuals, illegal content was uploaded to the document and it was reported; after being banned multiple times, it was eventually shifted to a channel format for management.
As independent gaming communities across the country gradually took shape and matured, Sha Lu’s outlook began to change. Especially after being diagnosed with leukemia, he felt it was time to focus more on himself: “Now that everyone else is up and running, I think it’s time for me to step back.”

Shalu occasionally encounters stubborn developers who, when he points out issues with their games and offers suggestions for optimization, show no appreciation; instead, they accuse him of trying to sabotage them and claim he can’t stand seeing others’ games succeed.He has also seen situations in publishing partnerships where developers refused to allow the publisher to interfere with the creative process, resulting in problems after the game’s launch.

In July 2026, independent game developer Sha Lu had just completed her sixth round of chemotherapy and was still facing a 25% mortality rate.

He had been ill for a year. A year earlier, in July 2025, Sha Lu traveled to Beijing to attend the Nuclear Fusion Game Expo.During the expo, he felt weak, but he never even considered the possibility of a serious illness. Looking back, he only belatedly realized how dangerous the situation had been at the time; if he had been jostled in the crowded venue of the Beijing Nuclear Fusion Expo, “he would very likely have died on the spot.”

After the trade show was over, Sha Lu went to the hospital, where the doctor immediately admitted him; he was subsequently diagnosed with acute leukemia.

In the early stages of his illness, his condition deteriorated very rapidly. At one point, Sha Lu fell into a semi-comatose state that lasted for a month. “I had to lie in bed for more than 18 hours a day and could barely stay awake,” he said. During that month or so, he completely lost the ability to care for himself, had no time to attend to the company’s future arrangements, and even experienced two life-threatening episodes.

After his health improved slightly and he regained his ability to care for himself, Sha Lu returned to game development. He identifies as an ENTJ and believes he has a trait that makes it impossible for him to stop working: “Watching TikTok or short videos, or playing games, doesn’t necessarily bring me much joy—it’s work that brings me joy.””

01

Selling a House to Start a Business

In 1986, Sha Lu was born in Suzhou, Jiangsu. Growing up in a family of moderate means, he had access to high-quality single-player video games from an early age, such as *Phantom Sword of the Ghost City* and *The Knights of the Flame Dragon*, developed by Han Tang Studio in Taiwan, as well as *The Legend of Jin Yong’s Heroes*,*Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, and *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*.

These role-playing games had a profound influence on his aesthetic sense of gaming art. After entering high school, Shalu and several friends created accounts on Youxian.com and served as moderators for *The Age of Discovery*.He was responsible for editing game information and walkthroughs on the forum, which led him to study a great deal of geography. During a history class one day, Shalu gave a presentation to the entire class on the Age of Discovery and even earned praise from his history teacher.

After that, Sha Lu developed a keen interest in the cultural impact of video games and published an article in the school newspaper declaring that video games are the ninth art.

During his college years, this gaming enthusiast began transitioning into an indie game developer, running a gaming forum and dabbling in fan game production. Whenever he had a new idea, he would post recruitment notices on the forum to find artists, scriptwriters, and voice actors.Since fan game projects were developed on a volunteer basis—with members working purely out of interest—the teams were extremely unstable, and people would drop out every other day. Looking back on that experience, Sha Lu reflected, “A group that runs purely on passion is highly unlikely to make it to the end.”

When he first left college, he worked in other industries as well. He took 20,000 yuan from his parents as startup capital to launch his own business, selling clothing and anime merchandise, and he also capitalized on the e-commerce boom by opening a Taobao store.It was a boom period for the textile and apparel industry. Sha Lu would often ride his bicycle several kilometers to work. In the summer, when temperatures soared to over 30 degrees, he would sort through merchandise in stuffy warehouses, often ending up completely drenched in sweat.

Shalu’s autograph from the event

Although his body was exhausted, the positive feedback from the business kept coming in.Sha Lu said that compared to making games, this entrepreneurial journey didn’t feel particularly difficult. During this time, he met his current wife through the online game *Ragnarok*. The two formed a team and chatted in the game, gradually growing closer, and solidified their relationship after meeting in person at ChinaJoy in Shanghai.

The idea of making games began to stir within me once again. My wife is skilled at drawing, and Shalu handled the game design; together, the two of them spent six or seven years creating small text-adventure games.

It was August 2, 2018, and the sun was beating down on Shanghai’s Pudong district. At the bustling ChinaJoy venue in the International Exhibition Center, 32-year-old Sha Lu was chatting with a group of online friends in their twenties around a dining table when he announced to everyone that he would be closing his Taobao store—which he had run for many years—and switching careers to develop indie games.

Later, Sha Lu wrote in her blog: “I sold my house to raise money for game development. Unlike some big shots who own stacks of properties—selling one leaves them with ten more.”

02

Lose Everything

“The Ballad of the Knight,” a project launched in 2018, was the first harsh trial of Sha Lu’s career as an indie game developer.

Through a friend’s introduction, Shalu met a technical expert. At the start of the project, the team’s cost estimate was only half of what it ultimately turned out to be. However, the collaboration soon revealed problems: there was a lack of trust between the two parties, and communication was extremely difficult. In Shalu’s words, “It was like having Fan Bingbing as the ideal, Qiao Biluo as the bottom line, and an ET alien as reality.”

This technician lacked enthusiasm for developing single-player games. He repeatedly demanded that Shalu add an in-game store system, and he was also slacking off—often refusing to write code and skipping work for an entire day at a time. Shalu felt quite helpless about this: “He said he’d work at most two hours a day; if it went beyond two hours, he wouldn’t work because his efficiency would drop.He just sat there playing games all day.”

Since there were no game designers on the team, Sha Lu handled all the game design work single-handedly at the time. However, after he finished the design, the programmer told him he couldn’t understand it and demanded that Sha Lu figure it out on his own and redo it in a specified format; even the slightest deviation from the format would earn him a harsh scolding.Shalu had no choice but to push himself to the limit: “I could only sleep about four hours a day, six hours on weekends, and I handled everything else all by myself.”

Even so, he didn’t switch lead programmers midway through the project. After all, changing the lead programmer halfway through game development would mean scrapping all the code and starting the game from scratch—the sunk costs would be too high.

After months of restructuring and delays, *The Way of the Hero: A Wanderer’s Song* finally launched on September 21, 2020.At that time, Shalu was facing the dire situation of its account funds running dry; without a launch, the company would not survive, so it had no choice but to brave the competition against *Xuanyuan Sword*, released in October, and *Cyberpunk 2077*, released in November.

The current Steam homepage for “The Way of the Knight”

After the game was released, it briefly shot to the top of the New Releases and Region-Wide Best-Sellers charts. Just as Sha Lu was about to celebrate in the QQ group, a flood of negative reviews came pouring in, and the positive rating plummeted to 54%.According to Steam’s policies, games with an approval rating below 70% are demoted, and *The Way of the Knight* was immediately removed from the platform’s recommendations.

The main reasons for the negative reviews were motion sickness caused by the camera work and a save file bug. Although the Shalu team had conducted four rounds of testing and five rounds of revisions, to avoid spoilers, they limited the testers to a few trusted friends. The small sample size meant they failed to detect these critical issues.Faced with the negative reviews, the team was on pins and needles. One girl, unable to bear the pressure, retreated to the common lounge to cry. Shalu and the team released two updates in quick succession that afternoon to address the issues, and the approval rating painstakingly climbed back to 70% by 1:00 a.m.

“This time, I really experienced the thrill of a roller coaster like never before,” said Sha Lu, still shaken six years later as she revisited the topic. The game, into which she had poured her heart and soul, ultimately ended in a disastrous failure. “It was a total loss—we didn’t even recoup half of the costs.”

The Versatile Solo Traveler

Following the failure of *The Way of the Knight*, Sha Lu decided to start work on a new project. title: With the World Cup Final set for 3 a.m., NetEase’s Lingxi, Sanqi, and Mutong took the lead in suspending operations
text:
At 3:00 a.m. on July 20 (next Monday), the 2026 USA-Canada-Mexico World Cup final will pit defending champion Argentina against European champion Spain. Even though the match is taking place thousands of miles away, it has already sparked a competition among three domestic gaming companies to offer holiday perks.
NetEase: From “Conditional School Closures” to “Unconditional School Closures”
NetEase was the catalyst for this round of time-off perks. Before the semifinals, NetEase set a condition: if the French and Argentine national teams—with which it had signed contracts for three consecutive tournaments—met in the final, all employees would receive a half-day off on the morning of July 20. However, the French team lost 0–2 to Spain, so the condition was not met.
However, the situation took a sudden turn. NetEase subsequently announced that, regardless of the outcome, all employees would have the morning of July 20 off, accompanied by the caption: “In soccer, there are winners and losers, but passion knows no winner or loser.”
37 Interactive Entertainment: CEO Gives the Go-Ahead for the Holiday
37 Interactive Entertainment took a more decisive approach. On July 15, the company issued a direct announcement: All employees would receive a paid day off on the morning of July 20, with no need to clock in. There were no prerequisites. Rumor has it that the boss made the decision with just one sentence: “We’re giving everyone the day off because the World Cup final is in the early hours of that morning.”
According to reports, as early as the 2018 World Cup, 37 Interactive Entertainment had already implemented a policy allowing employees to arrive late. It is worth noting that 37 Interactive Entertainment has consistently maintained a policy of letting employees leave work two hours early on traditional holidays.
Lingxi Interactive Entertainment: The Third Company to Follow Suit, Also Featuring “CEO Privileges”
Lingxi Interactive has also joined the trend of granting time off, packaging it as a special gamified “dungeon quest” and announcing a half-day off for employees on the day of the World Cup final under the guise of “the CEO handing out perks.” The company’s official WeChat account stated, “We don’t know who will win the World Cup, but the important thing is that Lingxi is giving us the day off.”
AviaGames: We’re on vacation, too
AviaGames, a major player in the global expansion of skill-based gaming, has also announced that it will be closed on the morning of the 20th. AviaGames’ titles *Solitaire Clash* and *Bingo Tour* are extremely popular in North America and consistently rank in the top 10 of their respective genres.
Mutong Technology: Watching the Game Means Eating Well and Having Fun
Mutoon Technology has also just issued an announcement stating that all employees will have a half-day off on the morning of July 20. Mutoon also noted that Friday’s afternoon tea has been upgraded to a “World Cup snack pack,” encouraging employees to take it home to enjoy while watching the games.At the same time, Mutong didn’t forget to promote its own MLBB International Women’s Invitational (MWI) Finals, which will kick off this weekend.
As of now, five gaming companies—NetEase, 37 Interactive Entertainment, Lingxi Interactive Entertainment, AviaGames, and Mutong—have successively granted their employees time off on the morning of July 20, allowing them to sit back and watch the final whistle blow.
A History of Creative Vacation Policies at Game Companies
In fact, it’s nothing new for game companies to grant their employees temporary time off for special reasons.
In 2023, *Honkai: Star Rail* launched its open beta, and competitors took the day off to experience the game;In 2024, on the day *Black Myth: Wukong* launched, the game’s publisher, Gamera Games (now Gamirror Games), announced a one-day company-wide holiday, and each employee received a digital deluxe edition of the game.
There have also been reports of game companies overseas taking time off in connection with the release of major titles such as *Cyberpunk 2077* and *Elden Ring*.
Of course, offering time off is not only a way to “pamper employees,” but also part of an employer’s ongoing efforts to build a positive image. For game companies, people are their core asset. Granting a half-day off for the World Cup final helps boost employee goodwill and demonstrates the company’s robust benefits program.

title: Raked in approximately 4 billion yuan; player numbers increased 30-fold upon official launch; Founder: “We’ve made more money than we can ever spend.”
text:
Two years ago, I couldn’t understand why *Fantasy Beasts: Paru* suddenly became such a huge hit, and now, two years later, I’m even more baffled.
On July 10, version 1.0 of *Fantasy Beasts: Paru* officially launched.Considering that after the 2024 Paru craze subsided, the game’s peak concurrent users had consistently hovered between 30,000 and 50,000—even after two major updates—I had assumed the official release would merely serve to further boost the game’s popularity. To my surprise, however, it reached a peak of 860,000 concurrent users, which carries a certain sense of “expanding and strengthening to achieve new heights of glory.”
The surge in online players reflects more than just the enthusiasm of returning players; *Paru: Fantasy Beasts* also shot straight to third place on Steam’s global bestseller list, attracting a significant number of new players in the process. Meanwhile, developer Pocketpair officially announced on July 8 that *Paru: Fantasy Beasts* had surpassed 40 million total players.According to forecasts by the VGI platform, *Paloo*’s actual total sales on Steam are estimated to be around 24 million copies, with total revenue exceeding $550 million (approximately 3.72 billion RMB).
In the past, we often attributed the massive popularity of *Paloo* to two main factors. First, its Pokémon-style pet design quickly caught the attention of a large number of players, and given Game Freak’s inaction at the time, many players viewed supporting *Paloo* as a form of retaliation.
Of course, this overly aggressive “borrowing” eventually backfired: in September 2024, Nintendo and The Pokémon Company filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Pocketpair, seeking damages and the removal of the game from store shelves. However, with Pocketpair’s “precise adjustments” to the game’s content over the past two years,the release of the 1.0 official version appears to signal a premature victory of sorts.
Second, the ruthless exploitation typical of capitalists adds a unique flavor to the game,especially the mutual understanding (and mutual harm) between the “cattle and horses” and the “cattle and horses” themselves, which resonated deeply with audiences. Memes like “If you don’t do it, there are plenty of Parus who will” went viral on social media, breaking through community barriers and reaching an extremely broad audience.
However, looking back now at the massive success of Version 1.0, it seems to have no direct connection to either of the two lines of reasoning mentioned above.However, prior to the launch on the 10th, Game8 conducted an exclusive interview with John “Bucky” Buckley, Pocketpair’s Head of Publishing and PR. Combined with the “we’re not short on cash” attitude previously displayed by Pocketpair’s founder, this seems to offer some insight into the matter.
First of all, in Bucky’s view, *Paru* is indeed a multiplayer game, but it is definitely not a service-based game designed for “Gaas.”While many similar products have opted for a “GaaS” model to pursue sustainable operations, *Phantom Beasts: Paru* has chosen a more pure one-time purchase model—a healthy cycle characterized by “delivering the complete content in a single purchase—players naturally move on after finishing the game—no anxiety over content depleting too quickly—and natural player return following the launch of major updates.”
He said, “Throughout the entire Early Access period, whenever the number of Paru players dropped and people started clamoring that Paru was doomed, I would remind everyone, ‘This isn’t a subscription-based game,’ and that it shouldn’t be designed to require new content every week or every month.Even if we were to stop further development immediately after the official release, players could still enjoy the game as it is, with its existing content and structure. Of course, this doesn’t mean we won’t release updates after the official release—it just means we’ll give more careful consideration to what our next steps should be.”
Without the pressure of monetization, everyone on the development team can focus more fully on game development. This is why Paru’s player count always rebounds with each update; in fact, when the full version launched, Pocketpair was even able to deliver at least twice as much update content as the Early Access version—with patch notes alone exceeding 30 pages.
At the same time, they also have enough energy to tackle another, even more challenging problem: “How to develop games in line with players’ expectations, and how to incorporate that feedback and make changes.”
He gave a simple example: “When dealing with different fans and different types of requests, you should aim to satisfy as many of them as possible.”In our first few major updates, we created a small area called ‘Sakurajima.’ Players who enjoy ‘hopping in and out’ really liked it. But for hardcore players, they found it rather lackluster—they could probably burn through that content in an hour, so it was essentially meaningless to them.”
So when we were working on our first major winter update—*The Island That Fell from the Sky*—we really had to ask ourselves: How can we make this update appealing to both returning players and hardcore players?As it turned out, many players felt that adding an area where flying wasn’t allowed could be interesting. So we had to come up with a solution to prevent players from flying within that specific small area. This was something we had never considered before the Early Access launch, but since players wanted it, we set out to make it happen.”
Bucky concluded by saying that while the development team does need to listen to players, they must keep one thing in mind: no matter what changes they make, they should strive to ensure that both casual and hardcore players benefit from them.
Furthermore, the precise positioning of the Paru franchise (Super Stitch) allowed it to avoid direct competition with most major IPs and carve out a virtually unrivaled niche within a new market segment.For a long time, Paru was categorized as a pet-collecting game, but in fact, at the outset of development, the official positioning was “factory simulation game.”
“Paru’s initial idea was: What if there were a management game like *Satisfactory* that used a group of cute creatures instead of machines? Wouldn’t that be fun?“What if these little creatures weren’t just cookie-cutter workers, but unique individuals, and what if we added some collection elements? Wouldn’t that make it even more interesting?” From there, the concept naturally evolved into an open-world survival-building game. Although the initial concept has changed significantly, I believe the core idea—‘you and Paru building a factory together’—has remained consistent.”
However, it’s obvious that the videos circulating online—showing players mowing down the cute Paru with guns and then sending them to factories to be ruthlessly exploited—clearly capture the “game’s unique features” more succinctly. While these videos have helped Paru skyrocket in popularity, they’ve also led many people who haven’t played the game to form a misguided impression of it.
Bucky explained, “Players expected it to be a traditional pet-collecting game with a somewhat linear narrative, but we were actually making a survival-building game, so there was a conflict between the two. As a result, our first challenge was figuring out how to set ourselves apart and then build on that foundation.”
As for Paru’s future, Bucky didn’t provide a definitive answer. He said that the team is currently focusing on just one question: “What do players want from Paru that the current version of Paru may not be able to provide?”
“We now have *Palfarm*—this project came about very naturally. Since many players just wanted a cozy version of Pal, and the main game couldn’t really provide that experience, we decided to create a standalone indie game.Another example is the visual novel *More Than Just Pals*, which started out as an April Fools’ Day prank, but since so many fans wanted to play it, we decided to make it into a real game.Later this month, we’ll also be launching a Palru OCG card game, and in addition to the Palru mobile game currently in development, we have several other small projects in the works. This IP will continue to grow.”
That concludes Game8’s interview with Bucky, but while I was gathering information, I discovered that Pocketpair has been doing much more than that during this period. During this year’s GDC, Bucky also gave an exclusive interview to GamesRadar+, where—in addition to discussing the content of Version 1.0—he revealed a very important plan.
“We have no interest in building an IP empire. We’re already a very successful studio, and we just want to keep doing more—funding the projects we want to do, as well as those we think other studios would like to do but need a little help getting off the ground.”
This means that Takuro Mizobe, the founder of Pocketpair, is in no hurry to expand simply to ride the wave. Mizobe had previously acknowledged that the revenue generated by *Paru* was far more than a studio of their size could handle (reportedly, the studio had only 60 employees at the time), which is why they chose to pursue a publishing model.
Pocketpair will provide funding and publishing support for other indie games and has offered a term that is extremely rare in the industry: it will cover all development costs, recoup its investment from any profits, and then allow the developers to keep all additional revenue.Consequently, during Paru’s time at EA, at least four games were published by Pocketpair, including the SOC hit *Journey of the Wind*, which previously sold 2 million copies—and all funding came entirely from Paru.
This also explains why, after Paru went viral, Pocketpair did not rush into IP expansion but instead worked feverishly to update content until the game was officially launched in full.On the one hand, as the studio’s lifeblood, Paru demanded their full and wholehearted dedication and effort; consequently, both the scale and frequency of its updates far surpassed those of any comparable product. On the other hand, using capital to support promising studios and products opened up new possibilities for Pocketpair, freeing them from the need to relentlessly milk a single IP.
From this perspective, while Paru’s success may have been fraught with uncertainties and various coincidences, throughout these two years of the EA period, everything Pocketpair did was marked by unwavering determination and conviction.

Two years ago, I couldn’t understand why *Fantasy Beasts: Paru* suddenly became such a huge hit, and now, two years later, I’m even more baffled.

On July 10, version 1.0 of *Fantasy Beasts: Paru* officially launched.Considering that after the 2024 Paru craze subsided, the game’s peak concurrent users had consistently hovered between 30,000 and 50,000—even after two major updates—I had assumed the official release would merely serve to further boost the game’s popularity. To my surprise, however, it reached a peak of 860,000 concurrent users, which carries a certain sense of “expanding and strengthening to achieve new heights of glory.”

The surge in online players reflects more than just the enthusiasm of returning players; *Paru: Fantasy Beasts* also shot straight to third place on Steam’s global bestseller list, attracting a significant number of new players in the process. Meanwhile, developer Pocketpair officially announced on July 8 that *Paru: Fantasy Beasts* had surpassed 40 million total players.According to forecasts by the VGI platform, *Paloo*’s actual total sales on Steam are estimated to be around 24 million copies, with total revenue exceeding $550 million (approximately 3.72 billion RMB).

In the past, we often attributed the massive popularity of *Paloo* to two main factors. First, its Pokémon-style pet design quickly caught the attention of a large number of players, and given Game Freak’s inaction at the time, many players viewed supporting *Paloo* as a form of retaliation.

Of course, this overly aggressive “borrowing” eventually backfired: in September 2024, Nintendo and The Pokémon Company filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Pocketpair, seeking damages and the removal of the game from store shelves. However, with Pocketpair’s “precise adjustments” to the game’s content over the past two years,the release of the 1.0 official version appears to signal a premature victory of sorts.

Second, the ruthless exploitation typical of capitalists adds a unique flavor to the game,especially the mutual understanding (and mutual harm) between the “cattle and horses” and the “cattle and horses” themselves, which resonated deeply with audiences. Memes like “If you don’t do it, there are plenty of Parus who will” went viral on social media, breaking through community barriers and reaching an extremely broad audience.

However, looking back now at the massive success of Version 1.0, it seems to have no direct connection to either of the two lines of reasoning mentioned above.However, prior to the launch on the 10th, Game8 conducted an exclusive interview with John “Bucky” Buckley, Pocketpair’s Head of Publishing and PR. Combined with the “we’re not short on cash” attitude previously displayed by Pocketpair’s founder, this seems to offer some insight into the matter.

First of all, in Bucky’s view, *Paru* is indeed a multiplayer game, but it is definitely not a service-based game designed for “Gaas.”While many similar products have opted for a “GaaS” model to pursue sustainable operations, *Phantom Beasts: Paru* has chosen a more pure one-time purchase model—a healthy cycle characterized by “delivering the complete content in a single purchase—players naturally move on after finishing the game—no anxiety over content depleting too quickly—and natural player return following the launch of major updates.”

He said, “Throughout the entire Early Access period, whenever the number of Paru players dropped and people started clamoring that Paru was doomed, I would remind everyone, ‘This isn’t a subscription-based game,’ and that it shouldn’t be designed to require new content every week or every month.Even if we were to stop further development immediately after the official release, players could still enjoy the game as it is, with its existing content and structure. Of course, this doesn’t mean we won’t release updates after the official release—it just means we’ll give more careful consideration to what our next steps should be.”

Without the pressure of monetization, everyone on the development team can focus more fully on game development. This is why Paru’s player count always rebounds with each update; in fact, when the full version launched, Pocketpair was even able to deliver at least twice as much update content as the Early Access version—with patch notes alone exceeding 30 pages.

At the same time, they also have enough energy to tackle another, even more challenging problem: “How to develop games in line with players’ expectations, and how to incorporate that feedback and make changes.”

He gave a simple example: “When dealing with different fans and different types of requests, you should aim to satisfy as many of them as possible.”In our first few major updates, we created a small area called ‘Sakurajima.’ Players who enjoy ‘hopping in and out’ really liked it. But for hardcore players, they found it rather lackluster—they could probably burn through that content in an hour, so it was essentially meaningless to them.”

So when we were working on our first major winter update—*The Island That Fell from the Sky*—we really had to ask ourselves: How can we make this update appealing to both returning players and hardcore players?As it turned out, many players felt that adding an area where flying wasn’t allowed could be interesting. title: 《控制：共振》：蔚为壮观的芬兰故事会
author: 郝磅磅
text:
2019年，加利福尼亚微软剧院，人声鼎沸。你坐在台下，看着走上神坛的那个戴着眼镜的日本老汉，他捧着金闪闪的年度最佳奖杯，说着你听不懂的东洋话。坐在你前排的那个神似周传雄的另一个日本老哥，虽然没能拿下年度最佳的桂冠，但一年后，他的作品将会如同末日的预言般名满天下。
你和你的同事从北欧姗姗来迟，挤进喧闹的狂欢人群之中。一整夜，你们看着那些优秀的同行来来又去去。你们一共入围了八项提名。你暗自默念，我曾经有8次必胜的决心。好在最终你们拿到了最佳艺术指导奖项。你对着你的同事说道，七年，我只要七年，我要所有人都看见我们的野心。
2026年9月，Remedy宇宙的最新拼图《控制：共振》即将正式发售。感谢由Remedy Entertainment提供的评测码。尽管时间有限，我们未能品尝完游戏的全部内容，但在近20小时的游玩体验中，我们已然能管中窥豹本作的野心和它身上独具一格的魅力。
千仞山头更有山
毫不夸张地说，《控制：共振》很可能是今年画面表现最令人惊愕的游戏，没有之一。
博尔赫斯的短篇小说《通天塔图书馆》里曾经提及过一个用通风管与螺旋回廊组成的六边形图书馆。他说，宇宙应该就是这个样子，里面包含了这世界上所有的知识与图书。在本作中，你甚至能看到比这更为夸张与瑰丽的地图设计如同在义乌小商品市场批发一般分散在游戏的每一个章节之中。
如果说前作的奇观是向内求知——在那座树立在纽约曼哈顿区的太古屋，外表用冷战时期的冷峻与严肃进行装潢，内里却充斥着官僚主义与后现代精神的无限抽象，那么这次你的视野将向外探索，扩张到整个曼哈顿区域。
于是乎，在这座充满现代主义精神的纽约城，你将会看到：一条公路倒挂在摩天楼的侧面，只消你前去踏上，整个世界的重力就会绕着你旋转；街道的尽头不是天际线，而是空间褶皱形成的断崖。希斯、霉菌、以及更为庞大和神秘的新力量，把曼哈顿划分成彼此物理法则互不相同的区域。在这里，你会分别看见牛顿的万有引力定律、爱因斯坦狭义相对论中关于时间的叙述在这个世界黯然失色，沦为想象与奇观的背景板。
而以公园区为代表的异象景观更是出人意料。Remedy运用色彩在陆地生生造出了一片汪洋——大片又霉菌构成的青蓝色平铺于城市街道之间，高耸如云的霉菌墙矗立在区域的边缘，像伸手不可见的峭壁。巡逻于其中的怪物要么形似金鱼，摇曳这巨扇似的尾巴在空气中漂浮，要么是像墨菲特一样在所处地盘中盘旋。
除此之外，在深入地下的地图里，你也能很明显地感觉到设计师们在游戏中的各处天马行空般地炫技，以展示他们丰富且出众的创意才华。这一点在以地下通道中的共振体迷宫中尤为显著。
尽管有着教科书般的地图设计与艺术造诣，但在城区地图的游荡过程中，作为玩家，难免觉得这片地图给你的探索欲会随着奇观的适应而渐渐下降。但好在主角迪伦超级灵活的人物机动性很好地弥补了这一点。作为主角，你大部分时间都在空间中的Z轴跳跃、穿梭，俯瞰这座吊诡的城市，而非用双脚丈量这片大地。
七步之内，拳快
所谓士别一日，当刮目相看。七年之后，《控制》不仅将主角从姐姐杰西法登换成了迪伦法登，连战斗模式也从原来的第三人称设计转向了更带高速ACT与RPG要素的模式。
在本作中，迪伦拥有相当多拟态的武器可供选择，它们将对敌人分别造成不同的Debuff，诸如滞空、失衡等能够叠加技能树，为战斗带来更多的变化要素。你也可以携带最多三个奇物，来为自己叠加不同的BUFF，以适配更多的战斗场景。
世界中还存在着多种共振体，你可以将他们理解为各个支线的BOSS。这些怪物的设计形态各异。笔者姑且不在此着墨太多，因为他们要么设计实在太过惊艳，要么在见到他们之前，会经历一场极其精彩的地图探索。
在历经千辛万苦击败共振体后，你将分别从他们身上获得各式各样的新能力，他们有的能够给到你更适配地区地形的技能，以便你在后续的探索中更加轻松，有的能够为你带来全新的战技构筑，在面对某些敌人时能够带来超乎寻常的效果。
正所谓，七步之内拳快，七步之外拳又强又快。
或许有玩家朋友同我一样，在前作的怪谈任务中挣扎，尤其是当杰西被困在旅馆中，不知道如何打开房门时，不得不打开手机查看各大博主的攻略。在搞明白之后不得不拍疼大腿，原来真相如此简单。在本作中，同样有许许多多的任务设计依旧让人摸不着头脑，他们甚至出现在了主线剧情中。你依旧会出现在任务点徘徊数十分钟，为其焦躁不安。但偶然间触碰到一个莫名的关卡，仍能为你带来柳暗花明又一村般的体验。
当然，还是有相当一部分的任务是可以依靠枚举法来完成的。
不过每个人的任务卡点都各不相同，这一点上，恐怕就是见仁见智了。
笨办法，好办法，能解决问题就是真办法。
其中有一个名叫，是谁在歌唱的支线任务，最让我会心一笑。你需要收容一只卡拉OK机异象，它经年累月地吸引着房客们在它身边舞蹈，至死方休。你需要前去拿起话筒，跟着英文歌曲，逐字逐句地对应歌唱，方能阻止在它周围聚集的人群逐一倒下。搞笑的是，唱歌的是英文，你需要快速地翻译成中文，并选出对应选项。
这对于堪堪过了四级的我来说太难了。当然，也有可能是我会错了意，才闹出这般笑话。
总之，游戏中充斥大量让人忍俊不禁的次级支线，作为在这个吊诡世界的一丝笑料。此外，我也想当建议玩家朋友们多多处理游戏中的支线，他们往往会给你带来意想不到的惊喜与超强的地图探索位移技能。
我们一拍即合
我在翻阅资料的时候意外地发现了参与本作的投资商之一Annapurna。之所以提及他们，是因为他们曾经发行过诸多广受好评的游戏，诸如每个小众榜单都必须提及的神作《艾迪芬奇的记忆》以及诸多人的独立游戏白月光《画中世界》《Florence》《星际拓荒》等等一系列精品游戏。可以说，这是一家有着极高艺术追求的发行商。
和Remedy的强强联手，似乎也印证着本作的诸多潜力。
出于个中缘由，我无法在此谈论本作的游戏剧情。一方面，为玩家剧透，破坏本作的初体验实在让人于心不忍，另一方面，Remedy宇宙中时常给我一些“我看不懂，但令我大受震撼”的感官要素。
于此，我只能安慰自己，多感受，少理解。
从亮瀑镇到太古屋，再到今天的曼哈顿，Remedy相当痴迷于草蛇灰线的写法，伏笔能从十多年前的《量子破碎》《心灵杀手》埋到近年来的《控制》《心灵杀手2》等。他们共同构建了独属于Remedy的庞大怪谈叙事宇宙。
尽管他们自称本作是最适合的系列入坑之作，但我还是强烈建议在游玩本作前先抽空速通一下常年拥有低价折扣的前作《控制》，不然你将会错失许多让人会心一笑的瞬间。抑或者在本作的游戏主界面中选择观看前情提要，否则你一时将难以理解为什么迪伦要如此执着地寻找姐姐杰西，以及那个代理局长波普对杰西总有些莫名的依赖。
也许会在初入这个世界时，你会被一大堆莫名其妙的名词所叨扰，陷入疑惑的死循环里，但请你相信，这个世界上，迷人已经是最不起眼能够形容他们的语汇。你只需要抡起锤子，对那些阻碍你的希斯伙伴们大喊一句“80！80！”。
正所谓，曼哈顿没有繁文缛节，也没有人情世故，只有最纯粹的打打杀杀。
本作对于中国市场也颇有诚意，首发便搭载了全套的中文配音。仔细听来，搭配上游戏，颇有种译制片的既视感，仿佛置身于CCTV6，观看中配版的《盗梦空间》。
除此之外，游戏中还出现了来自中国的超自然现象机构以及异常神秘，来自中国沈阳的防盗门。尽管只是只言片语，但一想到也许五年，甚至十年后，一群像《一人之下》中各个身怀绝技的中国人在异象战场上驰骋，便让人不禁要大喊一句：
SHUT UP AND TAKE MY MONEY！
9月，正式拉开了下半年的大作之旅。很难想象大伙会在这几个月过上什么样幸福又忙碌的日子。前些日子，友人给我发了一张梗图，写着活到2027的诸多理由，里面填满了即将在明年发售的游戏大作。他向我激动地介绍它们。
我有些心不在焉地回应，脑海里实则在倒数《控制：共振》发售的日子。

2019年，加利福尼亚微软剧院，人声鼎沸。你坐在台下，看着走上神坛的那个戴着眼镜的日本老汉，他捧着金闪闪的年度最佳奖杯，说着你听不懂的东洋话。坐在你前排的那个神似周传雄的另一个日本老哥，虽然没能拿下年度最佳的桂冠，但一年后，他的作品将会如同末日的预言般名满天下。

你和你的同事从北欧姗姗来迟，挤进喧闹的狂欢人群之中。一整夜，你们看着那些优秀的同行来来又去去。你们一共入围了八项提名。你暗自默念，我曾经有8次必胜的决心。好在最终你们拿到了最佳艺术指导奖项。你对着你的同事说道，七年，我只要七年，我要所有人都看见我们的野心。

2026年9月，Remedy宇宙的最新拼图《控制：共振》即将正式发售。感谢由Remedy Entertainment提供的评测码。尽管时间有限，我们未能品尝完游戏的全部内容，但在近20小时的游玩体验中，我们已然能管中窥豹本作的野心和它身上独具一格的魅力。


千仞山头更有山

毫不夸张地说，《控制：共振》很可能是今年画面表现最令人惊愕的游戏，没有之一。

博尔赫斯的短篇小说《通天塔图书馆》里曾经提及过一个用通风管与螺旋回廊组成的六边形图书馆。他说，宇宙应该就是这个样子，里面包含了这世界上所有的知识与图书。在本作中，你甚至能看到比这更为夸张与瑰丽的地图设计如同在义乌小商品市场批发一般分散在游戏的每一个章节之中。

如果说前作的奇观是向内求知——在那座树立在纽约曼哈顿区的太古屋，外表用冷战时期的冷峻与严肃进行装潢，内里却充斥着官僚主义与后现代精神的无限抽象，那么这次你的视野将向外探索，扩张到整个曼哈顿区域。

于是乎，在这座充满现代主义精神的纽约城，你将会看到：一条公路倒挂在摩天楼的侧面，只消你前去踏上，整个世界的重力就会绕着你旋转；街道的尽头不是天际线，而是空间褶皱形成的断崖。希斯、霉菌、以及更为庞大和神秘的新力量，把曼哈顿划分成彼此物理法则互不相同的区域。在这里，你会分别看见牛顿的万有引力定律、爱因斯坦狭义相对论中关于时间的叙述在这个世界黯然失色，沦为想象与奇观的背景板。

而以公园区为代表的异象景观更是出人意料。Remedy运用色彩在陆地生生造出了一片汪洋——大片又霉菌构成的青蓝色平铺于城市街道之间，高耸如云的霉菌墙矗立在区域的边缘，像伸手不可见的峭壁。巡逻于其中的怪物要么形似金鱼，摇曳这巨扇似的尾巴在空气中漂浮，要么是像墨菲特一样在所处地盘中盘旋。

除此之外，在深入地下的地图里，你也能很明显地感觉到设计师们在游戏中的各处天马行空般地炫技，以展示他们丰富且出众的创意才华。这一点在以地下通道中的共振体迷宫中尤为显著。

尽管有着教科书般的地图设计与艺术造诣，但在城区地图的游荡过程中，作为玩家，难免觉得这片地图给你的探索欲会随着奇观的适应而渐渐下降。但好在主角迪伦超级灵活的人物机动性很好地弥补了这一点。作为主角，你大部分时间都在空间中的Z轴跳跃、穿梭，俯瞰这座吊诡的城市，而非用双脚丈量这片大地。


七步之内，拳快

所谓士别一日，当刮目相看。七年之后，《控制》不仅将主角从姐姐杰西法登换成了迪伦法登，连战斗模式也从原来的第三人称设计转向了更带高速ACT与RPG要素的模式。

在本作中，迪伦拥有相当多拟态的武器可供选择，它们将对敌人分别造成不同的Debuff，诸如滞空、失衡等能够叠加技能树，为战斗带来更多的变化要素。你也可以携带最多三个奇物，来为自己叠加不同的BUFF，以适配更多的战斗场景。

世界中还存在着多种共振体，你可以将他们理解为各个支线的BOSS。这些怪物的设计形态各异。笔者姑且不在此着墨太多，因为他们要么设计实在太过惊艳，要么在见到他们之前，会经历一场极其精彩的地图探索。

在历经千辛万苦击败共振体后，你将分别从他们身上获得各式各样的新能力，他们有的能够给到你更适配地区地形的技能，以便你在后续的探索中更加轻松，有的能够为你带来全新的战技构筑，在面对某些敌人时能够带来超乎寻常的效果。

正所谓，七步之内拳快，七步之外拳又强又快。

或许有玩家朋友同我一样，在前作的怪谈任务中挣扎，尤其是当杰西被困在旅馆中，不知道如何打开房门时，不得不打开手机查看各大博主的攻略。在搞明白之后不得不拍疼大腿，原来真相如此简单。在本作中，同样有许许多多的任务设计依旧让人摸不着头脑，他们甚至出现在了主线剧情中。你依旧会出现在任务点徘徊数十分钟，为其焦躁不安。但偶然间触碰到一个莫名的关卡，仍能为你带来柳暗花明又一村般的体验。

当然，还是有相当一部分的任务是可以依靠枚举法来完成的。

不过每个人的任务卡点都各不相同，这一点上，恐怕就是见仁见智了。

笨办法，好办法，能解决问题就是真办法。

其中有一个名叫，是谁在歌唱的支线任务，最让我会心一笑。你需要收容一只卡拉OK机异象，它经年累月地吸引着房客们在它身边舞蹈，至死方休。你需要前去拿起话筒，跟着英文歌曲，逐字逐句地对应歌唱，方能阻止在它周围聚集的人群逐一倒下。搞笑的是，唱歌的是英文，你需要快速地翻译成中文，并选出对应选项。

这对于堪堪过了四级的我来说太难了。当然，也有可能是我会错了意，才闹出这般笑话。

总之，游戏中充斥大量让人忍俊不禁的次级支线，作为在这个吊诡世界的一丝笑料。此外，我也想当建议玩家朋友们多多处理游戏中的支线，他们往往会给你带来意想不到的惊喜与超强的地图探索位移技能。


我们一拍即合

我在翻阅资料的时候意外地发现了参与本作的投资商之一Annapurna。之所以提及他们，是因为他们曾经发行过诸多广受好评的游戏，诸如每个小众榜单都必须提及的神作《艾迪芬奇的记忆》以及诸多人的独立游戏白月光《画中世界》《Florence》《星际拓荒》等等一系列精品游戏。可以说，这是一家有着极高艺术追求的发行商。

和Remedy的强强联手，似乎也印证着本作的诸多潜力。

出于个中缘由，我无法在此谈论本作的游戏剧情。一方面，为玩家剧透，破坏本作的初体验实在让人于心不忍，另一方面，Remedy宇宙中时常给我一些“我看不懂，但令我大受震撼”的感官要素。

于此，我只能安慰自己，多感受，少理解。

从亮瀑镇到太古屋，再到今天的曼哈顿，Remedy相当痴迷于草蛇灰线的写法，伏笔能从十多年前的《量子破碎》《心灵杀手》埋到近年来的《控制》《心灵杀手2》等。他们共同构建了独属于Remedy的庞大怪谈叙事宇宙。

尽管他们自称本作是最适合的系列入坑之作，但我还是强烈建议在游玩本作前先抽空速通一下常年拥有低价折扣的前作《控制》，不然你将会错失许多让人会心一笑的瞬间。抑或者在本作的游戏主界面中选择观看前情提要，否则你一时将难以理解为什么迪伦要如此执着地寻找姐姐杰西，以及那个代理局长波普对杰西总有些莫名的依赖。

也许会在初入这个世界时，你会被一大堆莫名其妙的名词所叨扰，陷入疑惑的死循环里，但请你相信，这个世界上，迷人已经是最不起眼能够形容他们的语汇。你只需要抡起锤子，对那些阻碍你的希斯伙伴们大喊一句“80！80！”。

正所谓，曼哈顿没有繁文缛节，也没有人情世故，只有最纯粹的打打杀杀。

本作对于中国市场也颇有诚意，首发便搭载了全套的中文配音。仔细听来，搭配上游戏，颇有种译制片的既视感，仿佛置身于CCTV6，观看中配版的《盗梦空间》。

除此之外，游戏中还出现了来自中国的超自然现象机构以及异常神秘，来自中国沈阳的防盗门。尽管只是只言片语，但一想到也许五年，甚至十年后，一群像《一人之下》中各个身怀绝技的中国人在异象战场上驰骋，便让人不禁要大喊一句：

SHUT UP AND TAKE MY MONEY！

9月，正式拉开了下半年的大作之旅。很难想象大伙会在这几个月过上什么样幸福又忙碌的日子。前些日子，友人给我发了一张梗图，写着活到2027的诸多理由，里面填满了即将在明年发售的游戏大作。他向我激动地介绍它们。

我有些心不在焉地回应，脑海里实则在倒数《控制：共振》发售的日子。

title: Control Resonant | Critical Consensus
author: Sophie McEvoy
excerpt:
Seven years after launching Control, Remedy returns to a paranatural Manhattan with Control Resonant.
Read more
text:
Seven years after launching Control, Remedy returns to a paranatural Manhattan with Control Resonant.
Remedy has called Resonant a " not so safe sequel ," a perception some may attribute to the new protagonist . Players explore a paranatural Manhattan as Dylan Faden, the younger brother of Control's Jesse Faden, who has since disappeared.
Control's creative director, Mikael Kasurinen, envisioned early that the first two games would focus on each Faden sibling. Resonant departs from Remedy's established third-person shooter formula by introducing a melee-focused, open-ended world .
This marks a bold shift for a studio with three decades of experience in a proven genre, but early critical response indicates success with a score of 84 on Metacritic .
"[Resonant is] driven along by strong character-first storytelling and Remedy's best action in ages" James Archer, Rock Paper Shotgun
For Rock Paper Shotgun 's James Archer, the studio's "gamble pays off spectacularly."
"Resonant's reality-bending trip across a kaleidoscopic Manhattan is as rich in stark views, eerie atmosphere, and creative quests as Control's Oldest House ever was, driven along by strong character-first storytelling and Remedy's best action in ages."
Kotaku 's Cole Kronman held similar sentiments. "This is, without a doubt, the most demanding, most video-game-per-square-inch video game Remedy has ever made. Imperfect, but relentlessly, characteristically interesting," he wrote.
"I won't pretend that Remedy is reinventing any wheels. But Control Resonant stands out in a sea of blockbuster releases whose storytelling instincts range from atrophied to nonexistent. Its narrative is built from the ground up for playability by designers concerned with, above all else, why video games should be video games."
Combat
The action centres on Dylan's affinity for melee and use of the Aberrant, a weapon that transforms into multiple types. In Michael Higham's 8 out of 10 review for IGN , he found that the combat was "undercooked in spots, but that doesn't sour everything around it. Frustrations aside, Remedy's first crack at this style of action combat is admirable because it's foundationally sound and does have fantastic moments of satisfaction that the genre greats pull off."
"If anything, the fights are simply a slick vehicle for building up Dylan as a character and funnelling you through one of the more inventive open worlds I've seen"
Eurogamer 's Alexis Ong, in her 3 out of 5 review, criticized Dylan's traversal abilities, which are used both in and out of combat, writing that it "plays out like Spider-Man helping literal puppies and saving civilians."
"[Control] was a game that understood the genres it drew from, and most importantly, knew what it wasn't (the combat systems weren't very good then, and they're still not great now, but let's be real – no one is playing Remedy games for the combat)."
However, Kotaku's Kronman found a "gratifying synergy in how the game applies movement to both combat and traversal – mastering one puts you well on your way to mastering the other."
The paranatural spreads from the Oldest House into Manhattan | Image credit: Remedy Entertainment
Open-ended Manhattan
The original Control contained its story inside the Oldest House, filled with shifting rooms, walls, and thresholds to alternative dimensions. In Resonant, Dylan enters an open-ended Manhattan, altered by an otherworldly entity that causes the city to fold in on itself.
The world is split into zones rather than a typical open world structure. Rock Paper Shotgun's Archer appreciated Remedy's take on earning XP and rewards in these zones, which level up as you fight enemies and complete side quests.
"It's a peculiar mechanism, but one that works. Tying power progression to time and effort spent in different areas motivates exploration, arguably more so than simply slathering the map in question marks, and in my mind creating a tidy, almost Elden Ring-like loop of 'Get rewards, challenge boss, get rewards.' Lending, in turn, a more tangible and digestible structure to the open world."
Related
Remedy rolls out last FBC: Firebreak content update, affirms the game will be online "for years to come"
"From all of us on the team, thank you for your own passion and experimentation, and we'll see you in there"
The change in setting shone for IGN's Higham, too. "The way the design language of The Oldest House has spilled into the streets gives it a personality that's so distinctly Control. The environment seamlessly guides you on what's what and where to go, so even in the absence of a more detailed map, I was rarely ever lost as long as I paid attention to my surroundings. This strikes a delicate balance, letting the world itself take the lead rather than waypointing every little thing."
"The way the design language of The Oldest House has spilled into the streets gives it a personality that's so distinctly Control" Michael Higham, IGN
"When you start to understand how these various planes converge and break from each other, I can only envy the genius of how it was designed and the headache it must have been to create, especially at this scope and scale. It's not just for show; even when it gets unwieldy, it adds depth and texture to what would've felt like a fairly standard world."
Kotaku's Kronman described The Pattern (the force affecting Manhattan's geometry) as "a visual and technical marvel."
"Remedy has fully embraced the notion of video games as interactive art exhibits, designing environments under the guiding principle that 3D art and 3D level geometry can be the exact same thing," Kronman wrote.
"There is nothing else that plays quite like this because there is nothing else that looks quite like this—the case for Remedy, once again, is that they understand on a bone-deep level what makes this medium interesting, and pursue their vision with a fervor begotten of generosity. They made Resonant because they want us to understand, too."
But for Eurogamer's Ong, leaving the Oldest House removed the innate weirdness of what it contained.
"The Oldest House was a moody, ancient Brutalist cocoon full of secrets – you couldn't trust the walls around you, which was a neat setting for getting sucked into the bowels of a government agency," she wrote. "There's only so much you can do to spice up a repeated landscape of city blocks and same-y military blockades without losing aesthetic potency."
"After a certain point it feels like Resonant leans a bit too much on quirky weirdness in New York, as a stand-in for narrative quality and substance. Not much comes close to the 'oh shit, cool' moments or impeccable vibes that made Control special."
Boss battles
The main criticism of Resonant lay with the game's bosses. Critics highly praised the design and implementation, but were less impressed with the level design and combat.
"Encounter design is where Control Resonant falters most," wrote Higham. "Roughly half the bosses are spongy slogs that are less about testing your mastery and more about grinding out a war of attrition. Once you see their handful of tricks, you just have to rinse and repeat as you chip away at their health bar and hope you don't trip up in the repetitive cycle that it demands from you."
Rock Paper Shotgun's Archer agreed, considering them representative of "Remedy's character action inexperience."
"Some genuinely are enjoyable, one-on-one paranatural duels, though others are overly simple, their sense of threat owed to massive health bars and the sheer damage of their attacks – not the challenge of recognising and avoiding them. They do all have the striking and memorable visual design you'd want from an action-RPG boss, at least, and their reward of potentially build-altering new combat powers meant I never felt I was wasting my time going after them."
Control Resonant centers around the sibling bond of Jesse and Dylan Faden | Image credit: Remedy Entertainment
Narrative
Returning players will already be familiar with Dylan, who was host to the antagonistic Hiss entity in Control. But there's enough lore and explanation for new players to understand what he's been through, how the world reacts to him and how he reacts to it.
IGN's Higham found that Resonant acted both as a sequel and a prequel to Control through Dylan and Jesse, as it "tidies up a lot of what was either left to implication or collectible documents in Control," although he felt that the main story "relies on a few easy logical leaps to tidy things up, which means it may not be quite as moving in the grand scheme of the Remedyverse,"
Eurogamer's Ong attributed overall pacing issues in Resonant to its open-world structure.
"There's the usual triple-A dance between big save-the-world story beats and minor side stories where all the best writing is hidden" Alexis Ong, Eurogamer
"There's the usual triple-A dance between big save-the-world story beats and minor side stories where all the best writing is hidden, but at times, like when Zoe radios Dylan to do nothingburger tasks after a big urgent plot reveal, the pacing suffers. The cumulative effect is a kind of narrative sprawl, an inversion of the purpose that shaped Jesse's journey in Control."
Kotaku's Kronman felt that "dialogue is a bit hit-or-miss, something that could also be said of Control—there's a tendency here, endemic as well to much modern TV, to mistake snarky, too-clever-by-half banter for genuine characterization." He neverthless judged these "forgivable snags in what is, altogether, a thoughtful, effective story."
Overall consensus
Remedy's decision to move beyond its established formula was well received by critics.
"Surprisingly, this is one of Remedy's most conventional stories, but that doesn't mean it doesn't dare to be bold at times," sauid IGN's Higham. "Control Resonant is a game bolstered by a compilation of powerful moments – from the finer details in its superb world design to the twists that elevate its characters beyond the paranormal happenings that dictate their lives."
However, Eurogamer's Ong felt that Resonant is "chasing the hallmarks of a live-service game, only partly successfully, to echo the very deliberate structure and style of the genre storytelling that worked so well in the first game."
"It's not a question of giving us something we haven't seen before. It's a question of being able to sustain that distinct, uncanny weirdness that brought Control to life. And to expand on that core magic, without muddying what made it special in the first place."
But for Kotaku's Kronman, Resonant was what he needed it to be. "I was excited about Control Resonant because I thought I knew what to expect; now I'm excited about Control Resonant because I don't know what comes next."

Kotaku's Kronman described The Pattern (the force affecting Manhattan's geometry) as "a visual and technical marvel."

"There is nothing else that plays quite like this because there is nothing else that looks quite like this—the case for Remedy, once again, is that they understand on a bone-deep level what makes this medium interesting, and pursue their vision with a fervor begotten of generosity. They made Resonant because they want us to understand, too."

But for Eurogamer's Ong, leaving the Oldest House removed the innate weirdness of what it contained.

"The Oldest House was a moody, ancient Brutalist cocoon full of secrets – you couldn't trust the walls around you, which was a neat setting for getting sucked into the bowels of a government agency," she wrote. "There's only so much you can do to spice up a repeated landscape of city blocks and same-y military blockades without losing aesthetic potency."

"After a certain point it feels like Resonant leans a bit too much on quirky weirdness in New York, as a stand-in for narrative quality and substance. Not much comes close to the 'oh shit, cool' moments or impeccable vibes that made Control special."

Boss battles

The main criticism of Resonant lay with the game's bosses. Critics highly praised the design and implementation, but were less impressed with the level design and combat.

"Encounter design is where Control Resonant falters most," wrote Higham. "Roughly half the bosses are spongy slogs that are less about testing your mastery and more about grinding out a war of attrition. Once you see their handful of tricks, you just have to rinse and repeat as you chip away at their health bar and hope you don't trip up in the repetitive cycle that it demands from you."

Rock Paper Shotgun's Archer agreed, considering them representative of "Remedy's character action inexperience."

"Some genuinely are enjoyable, one-on-one paranatural duels, though others are overly simple, their sense of threat owed to massive health bars and the sheer damage of their attacks – not the challenge of recognising and avoiding them. They do all have the striking and memorable visual design you'd want from an action-RPG boss, at least, and their reward of potentially build-altering new combat powers meant I never felt I was wasting my time going after them."

Narrative

Returning players will already be familiar with Dylan, who was host to the antagonistic Hiss entity in Control. But there's enough lore and explanation for new players to understand what he's been through, how the world reacts to him and how he reacts to it.

IGN's Higham found that Resonant acted both as a sequel and a prequel to Control through Dylan and Jesse, as it "tidies up a lot of what was either left to implication or collectible documents in Control," although he felt that the main story "relies on a few easy logical leaps to tidy things up, which means it may not be quite as moving in the grand scheme of the Remedyverse,"

Eurogamer's Ong attributed overall pacing issues in Resonant to its open-world structure.

"There's the usual triple-A dance between big save-the-world story beats and minor side stories where all the best writing is hidden"

Alexis Ong, Eurogamer

"There's the usual triple-A dance between big save-the-world story beats and minor side stories where all the best writing is hidden, but at times, like when Zoe radios Dylan to do nothingburger tasks after a big urgent plot reveal, the pacing suffers. The cumulative effect is a kind of narrative sprawl, an inversion of the purpose that shaped Jesse's journey in Control."

Kotaku's Kronman felt that "dialogue is a bit hit-or-miss, something that could also be said of Control—there's a tendency here, endemic as well to much modern TV, to mistake snarky, too-clever-by-half banter for genuine characterization." He neverthless judged these "forgivable snags in what is, altogether, a thoughtful, effective story."

Overall consensus

Remedy's decision to move beyond its established formula was well received by critics.

"Surprisingly, this is one of Remedy's most conventional stories, but that doesn't mean it doesn't dare to be bold at times," sauid IGN's Higham. "Control Resonant is a game bolstered by a compilation of powerful moments – from the finer details in its superb world design to the twists that elevate its characters beyond the paranormal happenings that dictate their lives."

However, Eurogamer's Ong felt that Resonant is "chasing the hallmarks of a live-service game, only partly successfully, to echo the very deliberate structure and style of the genre storytelling that worked so well in the first game."

"It's not a question of giving us something we haven't seen before. It's a question of being able to sustain that distinct, uncanny weirdness that brought Control to life. And to expand on that core magic, without muddying what made it special in the first place."

But for Kotaku's Kronman, Resonant was what he needed it to be. "I was excited about Control Resonant because I thought I knew what to expect; now I'm excited about Control Resonant because I don't know what comes next."

title: 触乐本周行业大事：TGS2026开幕，《世界之外》前制作人璇子创业项目名称曝光，《影之刃零》愿望单突破300万份，《伊莫》Steam同时在线12万
author: 甄能达
text:
■ 史上最长展期TGS2026开幕，中国厂商规模缩减
9月17日，东京电玩展（TGS）2026正式开展。本届TGS正值TGS30周年，在展期上首次延长为9月17日至21日，为期5天，同时别启用了TKP东京湾幕张会馆，专门设立了面向亲子群体的Family Game Park。此前官方曾透露，预计本届TGS入场人数将突破30万人次。
展会上值得关注的新品包括R星《GTA6》，这款游戏在索尼展区搭建了大幅海报并设立了播片区，从商务日上午开始便因参与玩家数过多终止了整理券发放。同展区的《漫威金刚狼》《王牌空战8》《最终幻想VII：启示录》也都热度颇高。
此外本次展会上受玩家欢迎的游戏还包括世嘉《女神异闻录4 Revival》《暗喻幻想》《异于天堂》，SE《最终幻想7：启示》，Smilegate《MIRESI：看不见的未来》，《宝可梦》系列开发商GAME FREAK的二次元手游新作《雨のちハレ女》，三丽鸥旗下Sanrio Games《三丽鸥派对乐园》等，这几款游戏在展台规模、内容设置和试玩体验队伍长度上都十分突出。
TGS2026参展厂商名单
根据主办方此前公布的完整参展商名单，TGS2026共计759家厂商、3946个展位、覆盖51个国家和地区。其中，日本本土参展厂商484家，相较去年有所增长，海外参展厂商275家，较去年数量略有下降，但参展国家地区有所增加，来源更广。
本届TGS尤为特殊的一点在于中国厂商规模的变化。本届TGS中来自中国的参展厂商共计93家，其中中国台湾地区参展厂商为19家，中国台湾地区参展厂商为2家，整体数量均较去年有大幅度减少。也因此，相较于去年TGS现场引人瞩目的中国游戏大型展台和广告位，今年的TGS整体呈现的氛围和风貌都和过去有所不同。
■ 伽马数据发布8月游戏产业报告，《诡秘之主》首月流水超1亿元，《三角洲行动》iOS下载量最高
9月18日，伽马数据发布《2026年8月中国游戏产业月度报告》。报告显示，2026年8月，中国国内游戏市场实际销售收入为316.27亿元，环比增长1.7%，同比增长8.08%。
其中，中国客户端游戏市场实际销售收入达67.03亿元，环比下降2.34%，同比增长2.13%；中国移动游戏市场实际销售收入达到233.95亿元，环比增长1.39%，同比增长8.6%；中国自主研发游戏海外市场实际销售收入达20.30亿美元，环比增长0.88%，同比增长20.87%，继续实现同比、环比双增长。
中国自主研发游戏海外市场同比、环比双增长
除此之外，报告中还有一些值得关注的内容，如快手游戏旗下MMO游戏《诡秘之主》首月全平台流水超过1亿元，《英雄联盟手游》流水涨幅大增，《三角洲行动》为8月iOS下载量最高的游戏等。
■ 《世界之外》前制作人璇子创业项目名称曝光
资料显示，网易前制作人璇子创立的公司新注册了“于此降临”和“他于此降临”两个商标，这也被猜测为璇子开发的新女性向游戏的项目名称。
璇子为网易旗下乙女游戏《世界之外》前制作人。《世界之外》上线于2024年1月，凭借独特的无限流剧情获得了相当不错的关注，成为当时格局趋于稳定的国乙市场中的一个突出变量。
2025年10月，璇子从网易离职，创立广州执明网络科技，并获米哈游和Monolith（砺思资本）投资，公开资料显示，其公司产品定位2D、女性向、故事驱动游戏。
■ 《伊莫》上线PC端，首日Steam同时在线玩家数突破12万
9月16日，由FunPlus旗下爪印工作室研发的大世界捉宠RPG《伊莫》正式上线PC端，上线一小时内，Steam同时在线玩家数即超过10万人，首日突破12万。
在今年日益火热的大世界捉宠赛道，《伊莫》无疑是一款相当有差异化的产品，游戏采用偏写实的画风与真实风格的材质，整体主打减负，并设计了可以让玩家与“宠物”协作探索解谜的联结机制，以及与“宠物”高度关联的家园系统玩法等。这款游戏在早期便制定了全球发行的策略，从现有的Steam评论数来看，目前来自海外的玩家占据了相当大的游玩比重。
目前玩家已经可以在PC端游玩《伊莫》
此前，《伊莫》的全球预约用户数已经超过3000万，Steam愿望单数量超过100万。在前段时间的科隆游戏展期间，FunPlus首席商务官Chris Petrovic曾在接受媒体采访时表示，《伊莫》是FunPlus步入“第三阶段（跨平台阶段）”的代表性产品。
■ 叠纸法务部开通官号，点名诉祖龙、咪咕等不正当竞争案
9月17日，叠纸法务官方账号发布《叠纸游戏打击多种侵权行为取得阶段性进展》，表示公司已经建立系统性的知识产权保护与维权体系，并持续通过刑事、行政、民事等手段依法维权，后续该账号将持续关注案件进展，适时披露维权成果。
这是叠纸法务官方账号的首篇内容
这篇首发内容也重点提到了几起此前受到关注的案件，其涉及到的内容包括：
叠纸游戏诉说唱歌手王某侵犯名誉权案、诉祖龙不正当竞争案、诉咪咕不正当竞争案等多起案件均获得社会广泛关注。
在不久前宣判的一起游戏账号非法租售案件中，多名被告人非法获取大量公民个人信息批量注册《恋与深空》游戏账号，并使用外挂“养号”牟取不法利益。经法院审理，几名被告的行为构成侵犯公民个人信息罪、非法获取计算机信息系统数据罪，分别获刑一年三个月至四年五个月不等。
除该案外，针对侵犯商标权、侵犯著作权、不正当竞争、游戏泄密，以及恶意辱骂和造谣叠纸游戏及游戏玩家的行为，叠纸游戏均已通过多种途径开展维权行动，目前相关案件均处于司法进程中。
■ 《影之刃零》愿望单突破 300 万份
9月17日，国产动作游戏《影之刃零》官方宣布，本作全平台愿望单总量突破300万份，官方同步发布了庆祝贺图，向所有玩家表达感谢。
《影之刃零》官方贺图
《影之刃零》是由灵游坊（S-GAME）开发的暗黑武侠题材3A动作单机作品，采用虚幻5引擎制作，融合武侠与蒸汽朋克风格。主打高速连招、格挡博弈的动作战斗。作为关注度极高的国产买断制单机新作，《影之刃零》也是近年全球玩家期待度最高的国产动作游戏之一。
此前，《影之刃零》已在各大展会放出多段实机演示，并于8月12日开启全平台预购，国区标准版定价268元、豪华版328元。游戏定于2026年10月29日正式发售，同步登陆PS5以及PC（Steam、Epic、WeGame、TapTap PC）平台。
■ 《战狗》上线5天销量突破200万份
9月17日，《战狗》（Wardogs）开发商Bulkhead Interactive公布，游戏自抢先体验上线后仅5天，全平台销量突破200万份，官方同步放出庆祝公告。
《战狗》上线后市场表现十分火爆
《战狗》是近期FPS赛道的“黑马”。这款游戏在此前开启抢先体验，9月10日正式发售，首日销量突破125万套，目前已登顶Steam全球畅销榜。这款游戏由英国工作室Bulkhead Interactive开发、Team17发行，是一款支持最多100名玩家同局作战的战术沙盒FPS。玩家将分成三支队伍，在可破坏的大型战场争夺据点、积累资金，搭配步兵、载具、工事建造与地形破坏机制进行对抗。
此前，《战狗》的开发商Bulkhead工作室曾在2022年被腾讯旗下Splash Damage收购，《战狗》项目在这一阶段立项开发。团队原本计划控制项目预算，而腾讯希望将项目扩编成体量更大的长线服务型产品，双方开发理念存在分歧。2025年底，Bulkhead被Team17母公司Everplay和Hiro Capital组成的财团收购。
目前，随着《战狗》上线后市场表现火爆， Everplay也进一步增持了项目控股公司Super Media Group股份，持股比例从20%提升至28%。投资的增加，也意味着《Wardogs》后续可能会加大投入。目前，Bulkhead已经在游戏Steam页面承诺，《Wardogs》不会长期处于抢先体验阶段，主机版本计划于2028年推出。

9月17日，叠纸法务官方账号发布《叠纸游戏打击多种侵权行为取得阶段性进展》，表示公司已经建立系统性的知识产权保护与维权体系，并持续通过刑事、行政、民事等手段依法维权，后续该账号将持续关注案件进展，适时披露维权成果。

这篇首发内容也重点提到了几起此前受到关注的案件，其涉及到的内容包括：

叠纸游戏诉说唱歌手王某侵犯名誉权案、诉祖龙不正当竞争案、诉咪咕不正当竞争案等多起案件均获得社会广泛关注。

在不久前宣判的一起游戏账号非法租售案件中，多名被告人非法获取大量公民个人信息批量注册《恋与深空》游戏账号，并使用外挂“养号”牟取不法利益。经法院审理，几名被告的行为构成侵犯公民个人信息罪、非法获取计算机信息系统数据罪，分别获刑一年三个月至四年五个月不等。

除该案外，针对侵犯商标权、侵犯著作权、不正当竞争、游戏泄密，以及恶意辱骂和造谣叠纸游戏及游戏玩家的行为，叠纸游戏均已通过多种途径开展维权行动，目前相关案件均处于司法进程中。

■ 《影之刃零》愿望单突破 300 万份

9月17日，国产动作游戏《影之刃零》官方宣布，本作全平台愿望单总量突破300万份，官方同步发布了庆祝贺图，向所有玩家表达感谢。

《影之刃零》是由灵游坊（S-GAME）开发的暗黑武侠题材3A动作单机作品，采用虚幻5引擎制作，融合武侠与蒸汽朋克风格。主打高速连招、格挡博弈的动作战斗。作为关注度极高的国产买断制单机新作，《影之刃零》也是近年全球玩家期待度最高的国产动作游戏之一。

此前，《影之刃零》已在各大展会放出多段实机演示，并于8月12日开启全平台预购，国区标准版定价268元、豪华版328元。游戏定于2026年10月29日正式发售，同步登陆PS5以及PC（Steam、Epic、WeGame、TapTap PC）平台。

■ 《战狗》上线5天销量突破200万份

9月17日，《战狗》（Wardogs）开发商Bulkhead Interactive公布，游戏自抢先体验上线后仅5天，全平台销量突破200万份，官方同步放出庆祝公告。

《战狗》是近期FPS赛道的“黑马”。这款游戏在此前开启抢先体验，9月10日正式发售，首日销量突破125万套，目前已登顶Steam全球畅销榜。这款游戏由英国工作室Bulkhead Interactive开发、Team17发行，是一款支持最多100名玩家同局作战的战术沙盒FPS。玩家将分成三支队伍，在可破坏的大型战场争夺据点、积累资金，搭配步兵、载具、工事建造与地形破坏机制进行对抗。

此前，《战狗》的开发商Bulkhead工作室曾在2022年被腾讯旗下Splash Damage收购，《战狗》项目在这一阶段立项开发。团队原本计划控制项目预算，而腾讯希望将项目扩编成体量更大的长线服务型产品，双方开发理念存在分歧。2025年底，Bulkhead被Team17母公司Everplay和Hiro Capital组成的财团收购。

目前，随着《战狗》上线后市场表现火爆， Everplay也进一步增持了项目控股公司Super Media Group股份，持股比例从20%提升至28%。投资的增加，也意味着《Wardogs》后续可能会加大投入。目前，Bulkhead已经在游戏Steam页面承诺，《Wardogs》不会长期处于抢先体验阶段，主机版本计划于2028年推出。

title: A Lot Of People Are Seemingly Taking Time Off Work To Play GTA 6. Are You?
author: Eddie Makuch
text:
BambooHR , a human resources company that provides software-as-a-service for more than 30,000 companies, has released data that suggests people are taking time off to play GTA 6 this November.
You might have seen anecdotes online, or even stories from people you know in real life, about skipping work on November 19 to play GTA 6. BambooHR's data, though, shows a more concrete trend.
Why work when you can play GTA 6?
Using paid time off (PTO) data from active employees in the US, BambooHR found that PTO requests for the third Thursday of November this year--the day that GTA 6 launches--are running 9-17% above historical averages from recent years.
This data is consistent "at every checkpoint we can measure," the company said in a memo sent to GameSpot.
GTA 6 launches on a Thursday. There is no word on PTO data for the following day, but who wants to go back to work on a Friday? I would theorize people might book that day off, too, but BambooHR didn't share any data for this. A playthrough of the game can take 80 hours to complete , so it's good at least that people can roll right into the weekend and keep playing.
BambooHR acknowledged that it cannot definitively say that GTA 6 is the reason for the increased PTO for November 19. However, the company said the data does show a "real, reproducible signal." Who knows? Maybe people are booking time off from work to play Witch the Showdown in early access, which is also releasing that day.
Or perhaps people are taking time off work to celebrate the births of Jodie Foster and Adam Driver. Maybe people want to mark the 406th anniversary of the Mayflower reaching Cape Cod, or the 163rd anniversary of the Gettysburg Address. We just can't know.
In any event, GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Also launching that day is GTA 6: The Album, which features 34 songs written for the game from a range of famous artists. Unlike the game, the album will be on a disc .

title: Sony’s Iconic PS4 Game-Sharing Meme Has Been Recreated To Capture Our Depressing Future
author: Darryn Bonthuys
text:
Thirteen years ago, Sony "won" E3 with a simple public service announcement that dunked on Microsoft's controversial Xbox One DRM plans. All it took was 22 seconds for Sony's Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes to show how game sharing would work on the PS4, resulting in a huge PR win for the company. Fast-forward to 2026, and at the Tokyo Game Show, Yoshida and Boyes reunited to recreate that meme, but with a big difference: This time, there's no disc to pass between friends.
https://twitter.com/yosp/status/2100797688271012195
The original video from Sony--which was infamously put together at the last second--showed just how easy it was for PS4 owners to share physical games, compared with the frequent DRM checks that were initially planned for Xbox One games. Boyes left Sony in 2016, while Yoshida said he was "fired" from his role as SIE worldwide president in 2019, and he departed in 2025 after several years of leading Sony's Independent Developer Initiative.
https://youtu.be/kWSIFh8ICaA
Things have changed drastically since the two left, as Sony announced several months ago that it would cease production of game discs , an announcement that has not gone over well with its users and third-party partners. Sony's reasoning is that with the lion's share of game sales being digital, it can afford to move toward an all-digital future, which also has several positive knock-on effects for its business.
By making its PlayStation Store the only game in town, it can earn more from first-party sales and cut out the retail costs associated with physical games. There are fears that this could be a step backwards compared to a platform like Steam. Sony's PlayStation Store typically offers no refunds on purchased games and lacks several other features that would help make the transition easier.
The other elephant in the room is that you're not purchasing a game from its store, but a license to play it. Sony is currently arguing in a class-action lawsuit filed against it  that it doesn't mislead customers into purchasing digital game licenses, as it claims that it's "not plausible" for consumers to think they own their digital products. In comparison, Microsoft's disc-to-digital program has been received positively, as it allows Xbox owners to unlock a digital license for their physical games--but not all games, as some publishers haven't joined the program.

title: People Can’t Stop Talking About Mario’s New Tiny Pockets
author: Levi Winslow
text:
Nintendo recently held two Direct presentations back to back, with fans hoping that the company would reveal a new Mario game of some kind. While that didn't happen, what we did get was the reveal that Mario Kart World is getting some new tracks. Now, though, it seems the company has some more Mario news for us: new logos and renders for everyone's favorite mustachioed plumber.
It seems that over the last day or so, Nintendo quietly updated the look of the "Super Mario" logo. Honestly, the change is subtle . The colors are the same, just a little less vibrant and a little more gradient. The logo is also on one line instead of stacked, as it has been for the last 30 years or so.
The big "change," though, is in Mario's look. In a passing glance, you might not notice anything different. The mustache is still there. The gloves haven't gone anywhere. The hat looks the same. Everything appears to be in order. But look closer.
https://twitter.com/Swag_K1RBY/status/2100773081853608419
It's tiny, but on his waist is a ... pocket? Yes, Nintendo added functional pockets to the red plumber's overalls, which is great! I always wondered where those flowers and mushrooms went, and now it makes sense. He just stores them in his small pockets.
Unfortunately, if he had a Kingdom Phone--or whatever the smartphone equivalent would be in the Mushroom Kingdom--I'm sure that wouldn't fit in these pockets, especially if it was a foldable device like the newly announced iPhone Duo. I guess Mario can't play Mario Kart Tour before it shuts down forever on September 29.
Those pockets are also so itty-bitty that he probably couldn't hold many Nintendo Switch game cartridges. Not that it matters much, since there aren't any new 3D Mario games coming to the Switch 2 right now.
The internet is having an extensive conversation about what this means. Some believe that the new renders give Mario a more detailed look , while others are hoping we'll see our mustachioed plumber in 4K in 2027 . The main thought people are having, though, is that Nintendo finally remembered Mario.
https://twitter.com/jr_taurus62289/status/2100774237526982677
Even YouTuber GameXplain posted a brief overview video of the new renders , talking about how the clothing "just looks way better" because it doesn't seem like Mario's wearing latex. The texture makes our favorite plumber's clothing appear real.
All of this is great, but what would be better is if Nintendo announced a new 3D Mario game. The theory is that the company has something in the works, but nothing has been officially announced yet. These new renders certainly don't confirm anything, but with Mario getting an updated look, we can at least assume that this version of Mario will appear in whatever the next Mario game is.

title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Could Take 100 Hours To Beat, And Its Director Has Done It 46 Times
author: Darryn Bonthuys
text:
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is shaping up to be the biggest entry in the remake trilogy by a considerable margin, as game director Naoki Hamaguchi estimates that a complete playthrough of everything that the game has to offer could take up to 100 hours. That includes the campaign, side activities, and endgame content--something that Hamaguchi has experienced dozens of times for himself throughout the development of Revelation.
This is all part of the job; to ensure that players enjoy a smooth experience, the developers have to check every part of the game for any potential issues. "In a standard playthrough from beginning to end, if I were to review and check every single asset and element in the game, it'll easily take over a hundred hours," Hamaguchi said to GameSpot. "Obviously, I can't do that in each and every single playthrough. As the director, I don't have enough time for that, so sometimes I would just skip combat and focus on checking the main story. In different playthroughs, I focus on different elements."
In total, Hamaguchi said he had completed 46 playthroughs by the time he was interviewed. So how do you get so many game completions under your belt, when the game in question is so lengthy? Hamaguchi explained that he'd devoted all his time to playtesting the game, and he even slipped in a few testing sessions between interviews on the current Final Fantasy 7 Revelation press tour.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LRA759MHPJs
"I will try to do these playthroughs as much time as time allows," he said. "Yesterday, during a separate round of interviews, when there was downtime, I actually did bring a PS5 controller, so I checked the latest version of the build. Even on business trips, if there's even a small amount of time that I have available, I'll try to check the latest version of the game to see if there are any issues."
While Final Fantasy 7 Revelation might monopolize all your attention when it launches, the team at Square Enix also wants to respect your time. Minigames aren't essential to the game's main campaign, you can skip through cutscenes if you want, and pacing has also been adjusted to keep the story moving. For more on the game, you can check out how Red XIII might steal the spotlight during the snowboarding minigame, why The Witcher 3 continues to inspire Hamaguchi, and what Chadley will be up to in the game.
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch 2 on April 8, 2027.
Interview conducted by Emma Fyffe.

title: Very Large Man Could Join Helldivers Movie After A Different Very Large (Aqua)Man Dropped Out
author: Eddie Makuch
text:
Sony's upcoming Helldivers movie remains in development, and now a key piece of news has surfaced. According to Deadline , Reacher star Alan Ritchson will replace Jason Momoa as the lead, following Momoa's departure earlier this year .
Justin Lin, known for his work on the Fast & Furious and Star Trek franchises, remains attached to the Helldivers movie as director.
Alan Ritchson in Reacher.
The movie is set for release in theaters on November 10, 2027. Ritchson is reportedly going to play one of the helldivers, with other cast to be revealed later. Shams Jorjani, the CEO of Helldivers developer Arrowhead, has said he hopes the movie violently kills off celebrities .
Beyond the Helldivers movie, Ritchson has said he's a big fan of Activision's Call of Duty franchise and would be up for a role in the upcoming movie .
While Momoa won't be in the Helldivers movie, he is set to appear in October's Street Fighter movie as Blanka . Momoa is also coming back for the A Minecraft Movie sequel in 2027 , so he's not hurting for roles in video game movies.
Helldivers 2 was released in 2024 and became an enormous success, reportedly selling more than 20 million copies . Arrowhead Studios has said it doesn't, and shouldn't , have final say in how the movie turns out.

title: Ex-Naughty Dog Dev Apologizes To God Of War Studio For What He Said About Laufey
author: Eddie Makuch
text:
Bruce Straley, best known for his work at Naughty Dog on the Uncharted and The Last of Us franchises, has apologized to God of War: Laufey studio Santa Monica Studio, after he said he was "not excited" about what the game was offering, at least in some respects.
Straley told Edge that he thinks "every pixel" in Laufey looks "mindblowing and that he is "blown away" by the lengths Santa Monica Studio went to. However, Straley said he is "not excited" by "what you're doing in the game."
Beyond Laufey, Straley said he feels there is "no opportunity to inject fresh, innovative ideas" in AAA games generally.
A scene from Straley's new game, Coven of the Chickenfoot.
In a new statement shared on social media , Straley said, "I want to apologize to the Laufey team for dragging you all into this uninvited and unnecessary negative attention." He said he was trying to make a point about his concerns about the AAA games industry generally, and acknowledged that he made a mistake by naming Laufey specifically.
"I have thoughts about what’s wrong & the possible serious harm done to our industry & how we might be able to fix it. But in trying to have a thoughtful conversation I stuck my foot in my mouth & mentioned Laufey, and that was my mistake," he said.
Straley said games like Half-Life 2, Gears of War, and BioShock--along with games he worked on, including Uncharted 2 and The Last of Us--"set the 'modern AAA' mold." He said these games felt like "they were trying to creative a new experience within AAA."
Secondarily, Straley observed that the quest for "games-as-a-service" in a bid to make the next Overwatch or Fortnite is "not a viable strategy and frankly shows these 'industry leaders' don't know their own brand."
Straley went on to say he believes the gaming industry is suffering from a "lack of good leadership, clear direction, and conviction from the people at the top." These people are in charge of the money, and therefore determine the stability of the business, he said. "I believe if they understand their brand, they could have honest, inspiring conversations with creators to steer our medium to innovate," Straley said.
Straley is now working on much smaller games than he made at Naughty Dog. His new independent studio, Wildflower Interactive, is working on the puzzle-platformer Coven of the Chickenfoot. The game has players taking on the role of an elderly witch named Gertie, who works alongside a "creature-companion" that Gertie cannot speak with. Instead, Gertie needs to "discover the creature's true intentions" in other ways, like through environmental storytelling.
Xbox was originally set to publish Coven of the Chickenfoot before dropping it, according to another developer . It's still in the works, backed by an unknown financier.

In a new statement shared on social media, Straley said, "I want to apologize to the Laufey team for dragging you all into this uninvited and unnecessary negative attention." "I have thoughts about what’s wrong & the possible serious harm done to our industry & how we might be able to fix it. But in trying to have a thoughtful conversation I stuck my foot in my mouth & mentioned Laufey, and that was my mistake," he said.

Straley said games like Half-Life 2, Gears of War, and BioShock--along with games he worked on, including Uncharted 2 and The Last of Us--"set the 'modern AAA' mold." He said these games felt like "they were trying to creative a new experience within AAA."

Secondarily, Straley observed that the quest for "games-as-a-service" in a bid to make the next Overwatch or Fortnite is "not a viable strategy and frankly shows these 'industry leaders' don't know their own brand."

Straley went on to say he believes the gaming industry is suffering from a "lack of good leadership, clear direction, and conviction from the people at the top." These people are in charge of the money, and therefore determine the stability of the business, he said. "I believe if they understand their brand, they could have honest, inspiring conversations with creators to steer our medium to innovate," Straley said.

Straley is now working on much smaller games than he made at Naughty Dog. His new independent studio, Wildflower Interactive, is working on the puzzle-platformer Coven of the Chickenfoot. The game has players taking on the role of an elderly witch named Gertie, who works alongside a "creature-companion" that Gertie cannot speak with. Instead, Gertie needs to "discover the creature's true intentions" in other ways, like through environmental storytelling.

Xbox was originally set to publish Coven of the Chickenfoot before dropping it, according to another developer. It's still in the works, backed by an unknown financier.

title: I Guess I’ll Delete Every PS5 Game I Own To Make Room For FF7 Revelation
author: Levi Winslow
text:
There are quite a few months until Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches on Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. But you're going to want to get your systems ready now because the download for the final showdown between Cloud and Sephiroth may be big.
According to a September 18 VGC Interview with game director Naoki Hamaguchi, the file size for Revelation will "probably" be absolutely massive. So huge, in fact, that Hamaguchi acknowledged that there was no way the game would fit on one--or even two or three--discs.
"In a word, yes. Things are still getting worked out, but it's probably going to be around 200GB of game," Hamaguchi said. "I understand there are a lot of opinions about this topic, but at the end of the day, the fact is we need to overcome the hardware to a certain extent."
2OOGB is pretty huge, especially when the base PS5 (which is what I still have, sue me) holds approximately 667GB of usable storage space. With many of the games I own clocking in just at or well over 100GB (like The Elder Scrolls Online, Ghost of Yotei, Infinity Nikki, and Mortal Shell 2), I'm already debating with myself what games I delete to make room for Cloud's big sword and Sephiroth's shampoo collection.
Although Hamaguchi knows that the absolutely gargantuan size of Revelation's download prevents the game from shipping on a disc, he still reiterated the team's commitment to some sort of physical release . What that is remains to be seen, but it is important to Square Enix.
"One thing I want to say is, even though the game will not be on the full disc, in the position we’re in, because discs may be dying out, or maybe staying, with Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, we definitely wanted to deliver some kind of physical product," Hamaguchi continued. "That was really important to us. Trust me!"
We don't have an official file size for Revelation, as the game doesn't come out until April 8, 2027. However, we do know that it could take about 100 hours to finish , and with two post-launch expansions starring Vincent and Sephiroth that may be the same size as Remake's Intermission DLC, I suspect Revelation will be enormous.

title: New Pokemon Plane Looks Incredible, Even Includes Themed Cups And Napkins
author: Eddie Makuch
text:
Japanese airline All Nippon Airways (ANA) has unveiled a Pokemon-themed airliner to celebrate the franchise's 30th anniversary this year, and it looks incredible.
The Green Pokemon Jet, as it's called, made its inaugural flight from Haneda to Honolulu today following a big unveiling event--you can see video and images below. The airplane goes well beyond simply getting a Pokemon wrap, though it does have that, too, featuring famous Pokemon like Bulbasaur, along with Pikachu. Because how can you have a Pokemon plane and not include Pikachu? Also on display is Browt, a newer Pokemon coming in Winds and Waves.
https://twitter.com/poke_times/status/2100896394277990526
Inside the aircraft, there are headrest covers, paper cups, and napkins containing Pokemon branding. Beyond that, people flying on it can watch and listen to Pokemon-themed in-flight entertainment, including Pokemon: The First Movie and the best-of soundtrack from the show (1997-2023).
https://twitter.com/FlyANA_official/status/2100827162341192183
In addition to Haneda, which is the busiest airport in Japan, the Pokemon plane will make stops at a variety of airports in Okinawa, Kyushu, and Shikoku.
https://twitter.com/ANA_travel_info/status/2100832382970626300
Pokemon was created in Japan, and this is not the first time we've seen a Pokemon plane. All the way back in 2000, Japan Airlines announced that its fleet of jets would include Pokemon characters printed on the sides for domestic flights, along with Pokemon-themed in-flight entertainment.
In 2024, ANA created a Pokemon-themed safety video , featuring the franchise's adorable little monsters teaching passengers how to stay safe during flights.
